25th May 2023 Keith O’Sullivan Published (Updated) 1.0 1.1 1.2 The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction for users to successfully navigate the interface within Comply. It will outline high level explanations of built in functionality including: 1. Overview 1.1. Purpose of this document • Menus and Sub-menus • Columns and Fields • Icons and Switches • Interactive content 2. Analytics The Analytics menu provides the user with a series of preconfigured analytics dashboards. These provide the user with real time data, and key insights relevant to both their current and historical returns. Out of the box, there are 11 preconfigured dashboards. These are covered below. 2.1. Global Filters of the screen. The Analytics screens, like most screens within Comply, can be filtered to display data by a defined suite of Filters. To access this, the user can click the filters buttons located at the top This opens the Global Filter options where the screens can then be filtered by: • Entities • Jurisdiction • Date Range • Status • Timelines • Return Type Default Filter By Default, the Global Filters are set to display insights and analytics by the Current Month. So unless the user changes these, the Filtered Date Period will be the current month. 2.2. The Dashboards The first 8 dashboards are currently active and available. The remaining 3 are currently in development and will offer additional reporting very soon. • Refunds Analysis • Transaction Validations • Returns Variance 3. Global Dashboard The Global Dashboard is a snapshot of the Company’s global returns status. This is the Count of all returns which are at status Submitted and where the return submission deadline is within the filtered date period. 3. SUBMITTED 4. SUBMITTED LATE This is the Count of all returns which are at status Submitted and for which the Date submitted is after the Return Submission deadline (i.e. late). And where the return submission deadline is within the filtered date period. Note: The Date Submitted to the Tax Office Column is not enabled by default, but can be added to the All Returns Table using the Edit Columns feature. 5. PROCESSING RISK This is an index which shows the risk of not completing the processing work and thus not submitting the tax return to the tax office on time. A higher index means a higher risk. The factors affecting risk are discussed on pages 11- 13 below. Note: the user can click into a return on the table and see the scores making up the processing risk for that return.

A higher index means a higher risk. The factors affecting risk are discussed on pages 11- 13 below. Note: the user can click into a return on the table and see the scores making up the processing risk for that return. The factors affecting the processing risk are: • Current Return Status (max 3 points) Current Return Status Points • Number of Days till the Submission Deadline (max 3 points) Days till the deadline Points 3.0 2.5 2.0 1.5 1.0 1.0 3.0 2.7 2.4 2.1 1.8 1.5 1.3 1.0 0.7 0.4 0.1 Data Due To Prepare To Review To Approve To Submit Submission Failed 10 or More • Whether the Current Return Action is Overdue (max 2 points) Current Return Action Overdue Points No Yes, Overdue with 1 day Yes, Overdue with 2 days 1.5 Yes, Overdue with 3 days or more • Whether a Submission Deadline was missed in the last 12 months (max 2 points) Submission deadline missed for previous returns of the same entity, jurisdiction and return type in the last 12 months Submission deadline missed Points No Yes This header shows a count of all returns with a return submission deadline within the filtered date period and which are with a Processing risk of 5 or higher. The user can chose to increase/decrease their risk aversion. E.g. The default risk setting is 5, this is set at the mid-point of the risk range of 1 – 10. “1” being if the user has a low tolerance for risk, and “10” being very risk averse (doesn’t like The user can also preconfigure their risk threshold via: risk). Settings> Default Values > Processing Index 6. Net VAT Position (Month to Date) This figure is the current liability related to the calculated returns within the selected date range in the global filters. This figure provides the user with the EUR Net VAT position for all liabilities and refunds that have been submitted to the tax authority. This figure is calculated based on the sum of the positive and negative Net VAT Position figures for all returns (regardless of jurisdiction and return frequency) at status “Submitted” in the period selected in the global filter. Note 1: The default date setting is the current month. Note 2: The user should be aware that if they change the filter to another period or remove the filter, the figures will adjust accordingly. 7. The Net VAT Position (Next 3 Days). This figure is the booked liability (returns already calculated and submitted) plus the estimated position on returns in all other statuses based on only the next 3 days (after today). Please Note: The filtered date period is not relevant to this calculation. 8. The Net VAT Position (Month Forecast). This figure is the combination of: ‘The Potential liability (and/or refund position)’ + ‘The Realised liability / refund position’ This is based on the filtered reporting period and status of the calculated returns. Calculation: plus • • The sum of the negative or positive Net VAT Position figures for all returns (regardless of jurisdiction and return frequency) in the filtered reporting period.

Calculation: plus • • The sum of the negative or positive Net VAT Position figures for all returns (regardless of jurisdiction and return frequency) in the filtered reporting period. The status of the returns in this period are “To Review, To Approve, To Submit, Submitted” the sum of the negative or positive Forecast Net VAT Position figures for all returns (regardless of jurisdiction and return frequency) in the filtered reporting period. The status of the returns in this period are “Data Due, To Prepare”. The Forecast Net VAT Position based on Data Due and To Prepare uses the average of the last 3 submitted returns regardless of whether they were submitted within the filtered period or not. Please Note: • The Net VAT Position (Month to Date), Net VAT Position (Next 3 days) and Net VAT Position (Month Forecast) figures include VAT returns where the Return Deadline is within the filtered period, irrespective of the jurisdiction and frequency of the return. • Forecast Net VAT Position (local currency) for a jurisdiction is calculated based on the average of the Net VAT Position values for the 3 VAT Returns that were submitted prior to this return for that jurisdiction. E.g. The Forecast Net VAT Position calculation takes the average of the Net VAT Position for a return from the 3 prior returns. If there was no Net VAT Position for any of the last 3 returns, then Comply will use the Forecast Net VAT Position figure from that return in place of the Net VAT Position in order to calculate the average NET VAT Position for the current return (Return A). • Forecast Net VAT Position (local currency) for an amended return is calculated based on the average figure from previous month values (not the same month values). Count any amendment return within the period as one of the 3 returns for the average calculation. • Forecast Net VAT Position figures for past returns do not get recalculated unless they are at status Data Due or To Prepare. • The Forecast Net VAT Position (LC) and Net VAT Position (LC) are converted to EUR figures based on the ECB FX Rate that existed on the date that the returns were created in the platform. 9. Purpose of this document The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction for users required to file Control Lists as part of their VAT Returns. 2. Configuration 2.1. Configure an Entity for Control Lists Note: A Corresponding VAT Return needs to be configured before this step. The following error will be displayed if no VAT Return exists. To configure the Control List, complete the following steps: 1. Go to the Settings menu. 2. Select Entity. 3. Select the relevant Entity to be configured. 4. Chose the jurisdiction (Slovakia) 5. Click Visit This Page. 6. Now go to the Return Type section. 7. Click the + button to add the new Return Type. 8. Select Control List from the Return Type drop-down menu. 9. Select the relevant Frequency. 10. Click Add. Note: Frequency Note: Frequency Validation If during onboarding, the user selects a The Frequency option available in the different frequency to that configured in drop-down menu will always match that of the excel file for the VAT Return, then an the existing corresponding VAT Return. Error will be displayed and the Frequency for the Control List will be automatically set to the same as the VAT Return. 2.2. Control List Scheduler Offset The scheduler for the Control List is automatically updated to assign an Offset Date from Data Due – To Prepare of 3 days. Reason: This aligns the Data Due date for the Control List with the To Review date of the VAT Return (and when the Transactions are copied to the Control List). Impact: By doing this, email notifications are not triggered to Data Providers for Control lists as the Control List file should not expect data to be uploaded. 3. Returns 3.1. Files 3.1.1. Upload Files in the Control List). It is important to note that adding/editing transactional data should be completed on the corresponding VAT Return (the changes made on the VAT Return will be automatically reflected With this in mind users are restricted from uploading Data Files for Returns on the Files page of a Control List. Only Supporting Documents can be uploaded to a Control List. 3.1.2. Deleted Files It is important to note that Data Files deleted from the Files page on a VAT Return will result in the system removing all transaction data from the associated Control List. Example: Before the Data File is deleted VAT Return: Control List: When a Data Provider/Preparer deletes the file from the VAT Return, a message is displayed to prompt the user that by deleting the file all associate transactions will be removed. After the Data File is deleted Once the Data File is deleted from the VAT Return, a few things happen. 1. The Control List status changes back from To Review to Data Due. 2. The Transactions Tab in the Control List is now blank as all Transactions have been removed. 3. The Audit History is updated to reflect the Deleted File o VAT Return: ▪ Return Log, shows Deleted File o Control List: ▪ Return Log – Return Status Change ▪ Transaction Log – Associated Transactions Removed Where NIL Returns are required, the user (Preparer or Reviewer) can enable/disable the NIL Return using the Toggle switch from the VAT Return. This automatically synchronises the same 3.2. NIL Returns action in the Control List. To do this: 1.

This automatically synchronises the same 3.2. NIL Returns action in the Control List. To do this: 1. Go to the relevant VAT Return. 2. Click the Green arrow to expand the return header options. 3. Turn on the Is Nil Return toggle. 4. Now open the associated Control List for the same period. The Nil Return toggle is automatically enabled. Please note: The Nil Return Toggle can only be enabled in the Control List if the Switch is Off in the VAT Return. I.e. You can have a VAT Return which in Not Nil, and a Control List which is Nil. 3.3. Rejected Returns If the Approver rejects the VAT return, the status changes from To Approve to To Prepare. This will Automatically change the status of the Control List in the following ways: Control List status: To Approve The Control List will automatically change from To Approve to To Prepare. Control List Status: To Submit The Control List will automatically change from To Submit to To Prepare. Control List Status: To Review Please note: If the status of the Control List is To Review, when the VAT Return is rejected, then the Control List status remains at To Review. 3.4. Return to “To Prepare” Status If the Preparer changes the status of the VAT Return back from To Review to To Prepare, then this automatically changes the Control List back to To Prepare. To do this: 1. Open the associated VAT Return for the same period. 2. Navigate to the Return Review screen. 3. Click the Return to “To Prepare” button. This automatically changes the status of the associated Control List in the following ways: Control List status: To Approve The Control List will automatically change from To Approve to To Prepare. Control List Status: To Submit The Control List will automatically change from To Submit to To Prepare. Control List Status: To Review Please note: If the status of the Control List is To Review, then the Control List status remains The user can send a Control List back to To Prepare also without impacting the associated VAT at To Review. Please Note: Return 3.5. Submitted Returns 3.5.1. Submitting Control Lists Control Lists cannot be Submitted before the associated VAT Return has been Submitted. If the user tries to do this, the following error will be displayed. 4. Transactions 4.1. Associated Transactions IMPORTANT TO NOTE: been set to a status of To Review. Transactions are only associated with/to the Control List after the associated VAT Return has This means the Transactions page on the Control List will only be populated after the Data Validation process has completed in the VAT Return and has been sent for Review. 4.2. Adding/Edit Restriction Please note it is not possible to Manually Add or Edit transactions in the Control List. The Add and Edit buttons on the Transactions screen on the VAT Return are not displayed on the Control List. This means, any additional transactions or edits to transactions must be done on the VAT Return. 4.3. Synchronising Added/Edited Transactions To Control List All transactions that have been either manually added or edited in the VAT Return are then automatically updated to reflect the latest list of transactions in the Control List (after Data Validation is completed and VAT Return is sent for Review. Edit Transaction in VAT Return: The edited transaction is then automatically updated in the associated Control List. 4.4.

Edit Transaction in VAT Return: The edited transaction is then automatically updated in the associated Control List. 4.4. No Data Validation on Control List To avoid the need for duplication of work, all changes to transactional data is processed in the VAT Return and then automatically synched to the associated Control List. This means there is no Data Validation on the Control List. Data Validation Tab not available in Control List: 5. Numerical Boxes 5.1. Editable Columns – EDIT and SAVE Options The Preparer or Reviewer can make relevant changes to single/multiple transactions in the 3. Click the icon beside the relevant return box. From here the user can select either a single or multiple transactions using the Tick Boxes to the left (or select all). following Return Boxes: • A2 • C1 • C2 To do this: 1. Go to Return Review. 2. Numerical Boxes. 4. Click the EDIT button. 5. The user can then edit the following columns: o Numeric Code of Goods o Type of Goods o Quantity of Goods o Unit Measure o Correction 6. Make the changes in the relevant columns/fields. o Use the APPLY ALL field if the changes are applicable across multiple selections. Once a change is made the system automatically assigns a Modification icon to the modified/updated transaction. 7. Click SAVE. 8. Click the Modification Icon. This displays a pop up showing the Old and New Values associated with the change and the user details. 5.2. Supplementary Returns on the following Return Boxes: A1, A2, B1, B2, B31, B32, C1, C2, D1 & D2 On Supplementary Returns only for Control Lists, a new Column “Correction Code” is displayed 6. Audit History 6.1. Associated Transactions From VAT Return The Audit History on the Control List displays logs (All Logs and Transaction Logs) identifying when associated Transactions were edited/uploaded to the VAT Return, and we automatically synched to the Control List. The Log will Include: • Date of Event • Event Group – Transaction Associated • User – User will be System Bot as these are auto synched from VAT Return. 6.2. Edits to Return Boxes All changes made to Return Boxes are recorded in the Audit History. Transactional changes will be displayed in both All Logs and Transaction Logs. The user can view and submit the completed Return via the XML file. To view this: 7. XML 1. Go to Return Review. 2. Select View Return.

15th Oct 2024 Keith O’Sullivan Published Comply: Returns Processing Overview Purpose of this document The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction on the processes for Uploading files to Comply. This will include: • Uploading Data Files for Return (For clients not using API for uploads) • Files uploaded (For Clients using API for Uploads) • Uploading Supporting Documents Comply: Returns Processing 1. Upload a Data File for Return (Non API) For clients not using an API to automatically upload their transactions into Comply, they will be required to manually upload a Data File (taken from their ERP system) into Comply. Based on configured Scheduler, the Data Provider (User in Comply responsible for uploading data) will be notified that Data is Due. When they log into Comply and visit the Returns Tab, they will see all the returns which are on a status of Data Due. 1. Navigate to the Returns Menu. 2. By default, the returns displayed will be all returns those assigned to you. Comply: Returns Processing Set a data range filter if you wish to display returns for a specific period only. 3. Click the return you wish to upload a Data File for Return for. For this example, I (as the Data Provider) am required to upload a date for the return ID 27. It is currently displaying as Data Due, it is for the Return Period April 2022, with a Return Deadline of 09/06/2022. This opens the Return details screen. Comply: Returns Processing 4. Upload the Data File. To select the file from its current location the user can: Note: Password protected files cannot be uploaded. • Drag and Drop a file • Click the Choose File button. 5. From the drop-down menu, select Data File for Return. Comply: Returns Processing 6. Once the Data File for Return is attached, click Upload. The file is then uploaded and goes through a data transformation process, which runs the data against the comply rules engine to ensure the data is in good order to run through Comply. Once complete, the return status changes to To Prepare. Comply: Returns Processing Based on the assigned due date for the Data Preparation step, a notification is sent to the Data Preparer (providing they have configured their notifications settings), and the Return will now be visible for them in their Returns section once they login. That completes the process for the Data Provider. Comply: Returns Processing 2. Upload a Data File for Return (API Users) For clients using APIs for data upload, it is key that during onboarding the Data Provider role is assigned to System Bot (as opposed to a physical user). This is generally configured during onboarding or by an Admin User. Security > User Roles All relevant client data (Transactions) will be uploaded via the API and pushed through preconfigured mapping and validation. The Return details will be made available to the Preparer and will have a status of To Prepare. 2.1. Return Statuses In Comply Clients using API to upload return data (Transactions) will only manually process returns in Comply which have a status of To Prepare. Upload a Supporting Document Uploading additional files which provide supporting information is possible, but this information is not used in the calculation or generation of the return. To do this: 1. In the files tab, click to Upload or Drag and Drop a file to add. 2. Select Supporting Document from the drop-down menu Depending on the file type, Supporting Document may be the only option. 3. Click Upload.

24th Nov 2022 Keith O’Sullivan Published The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction on the steps required to configure comply for a Company to file Intrastat Returns. 1. Introduction 1.1. What is Intrastat? (Sales) of goods/commodities. 1.2. Who does this apply to? INTRASTAT is the name given to the system for collecting statistics on the movement of goods, not services, between the Member States of the European Union (EU). This essentially means that organisations are required to report statistics on Arrivals (Purchases) and Dispatches All VAT Registered companies trading within the EU member countries only, who buy or sell goods/commodities where the values are above certain predefined thresholds. (These thresholds may vary by jurisdiction). 1.3. How often is an Intrastat Return required? The INTRASTAT declaration is required on a monthly basis. Please note: Submission deadlines vary by Jurisdiction. 1.4. What is required? There are 2 Types of Intrastat Return: • • Intrastat Arrivals – This is the fileable return on Purchases. Intrastat Dispatches – This is the fileable return on Sales. Both are not always required. It is possible that you may be required to complete 1 or both. 1.5. Simplified v’s Detailed Intrastat Returns Thresholds are set by each jurisdiction for both Arrivals (Purchases) and Dispatches (Sales). If a company exceeds any of these thresholds, then they are required to file a more detailed Intrastat Return. E.g. In Ireland the thresholds are set at €500,000 for Purchases and €635,000 for Sales. Please note, you may be required to file varying types and subtypes of Intrastat Returns. E.g. it is possible that you may be required to file a Simplified Intrastat Arrivals Return, but also a Detailed Intrastat Dispatches Return. 2. Onboarding 2.1. To manually map the mandatory fields… 1. Drag and drop the relevant client columns to the Comply columns. 2. Click NEXT to move to the next page. 3. Once all the mandatory fields have been mapped click next. Please note the following mapping options are Optional (more detailed instructions on these are available in the “Comply Onboarding” guide). Users can click Next on each screen to continue. 4. Click Save. Repeat if templates are required for the different return Types and Subtypes. 3. Configuring Intrastat for Existing Entities For existing entities who are set up in Comply, but whom are now required to file Intrastat returns. 3.1. Configure the Intrastat Return Types Existing entities can configure this by performing the following steps: 1. Open the Settings menu. 2. Select Entity. 3. On the Entity Details page, select the relevant Entity to be configured for Intrastat. 4. Click the Jurisdiction Country Details. 5. Click VISIT THIS PAGE. 6. On the Jurisdiction Details Screen, go to the Return Type section. 7. Click the green + button. This allows the user to add a new Return Type. 8. Select the relevant Intrastat Return Type from the Return Type drop-down menu. 9. Select the relevant Return Subtype. 10. Select a Frequency. Intrastat Returns will always be Monthly. This is generally Simplified or Detailed, but is based on Jurisdiction. E.g. Italy does not have Detailed Intrastat returns so only Simplified will be available from the drop-down. 11. Click ADD. A pop up message is displayed to confirm the new Return Type has been created. The new Return Type is displayed. Repeat these steps to create additional Intrastat Return types as required For example…. • • • Intrastat Arrivals Detailed Intrastat Dispatched Simplified Intrastat Dispatched Detailed Please note: these are jurisdictional and may or may not available by country. Once all relevant Intrastat Return types have been configured, you can now view the relevant details on the Return Details page. To do this… 12. Click the Intrastat Return type. 13.

Once all relevant Intrastat Return types have been configured, you can now view the relevant details on the Return Details page. To do this… 12. Click the Intrastat Return type. 13. Click VISIT THIS PAGE. The Returns Details page displays the following 3 Intrastat details: • The relevant Intrastat Returns • The Frequency of the Return (Which is Monthly). • The Return Subtype. Please Note: the next step to complete. The Returns are not displayed here yet, as they have not been assigned to a User Role. This is 3.2. Assign the new Return Type to a User Role This action can only be performed by an Admin user role. 1. Go to the Security Menu. 2. Click User Roles. 3. Select the relevant Jurisdiction. 4. Click the Green Down Arrow to expand the view to display all Return Types for that Jurisdiction. 5. Add the relevant user for each role. Please note: If the same user is to be assigned to all return types, simply select the user from the Apply to All drop down option. 6. Click the Submit button at the bottom of the page. 3.3. Viewing Returns on the Returns Details page. Now that the returns have been assigned to a user. That user can view the returns on the Returns Details page via the Entity section. Note: This process is available to Admin users only. 2. Overview There are 5 Mandatory roles in Comply: • Data Provider – person responsible for providing the data for the return. • Preparer – person responsible for preparing the return. • Reviewer – person responsible for reviewing the return. • Approver – person responsible for approving the return. • Submitter – person responsible for submitting the return. A user must be selected for each mandatory role in each jurisdiction There will be 2 versions of Comply offered to clients: • Managed Service – Where TBI Staff will manage a large proportion of the day-to-day task on behalf of the client. • Self Service – Where the client will manage most of the day-to-day tasks locally. In either case, these roles must be assigned to one of the following groups: • Client Staff • Taxback International (TBI) Staff • System Bot (for use when using API’s for Data Upload) Note 1: A Company could potentially consist of multiple jurisdictions. If so, roles/users should be assigned to tasks for each jurisdiction as required. Note 2: If the same roles/users are to perform the same tasks for each jurisdiction, the user can select the roles from the drop-down options beside “Apply to All”. 3. Set up User Roles To assign a role/user to a task: 1. Go to Menu. 2. Click Security. 3. Click on the User Roles sub-menu. 4. Click the Entity drop-down menu. This allows the user to manage the roles at Entity level. 5. Select the relevant Entity. The roles are now displayed for the selected Entity. The user has 2 options: • Assign users to roles which will apply to all jurisdictions. • Assign different users to roles for specific jurisdictions. 3.1. Assign User Roles to all Jurisdictions 1. Click the Select User drop-down menu for the relevant role at the Apply to All level. 2. Select whether the user is a Client, TBI Staff or System user. 3. Select the user to be assigned to that role. 4. Repeat these steps for each role. 5. Click Submit. Note 1 - It may be the case that the Preparer and Submitter is the same person, but there are rules built in to prevent the Preparer and Reviewer from being the same person. Note 2 – The Reviewer and Approver roles can be assigned to the system user which will automatically approve the return for that stage in the process. Note 3 – Additional non-mandatory roles are also available for completion, these are: • Payment Approver – Applies to TBI Pay service. • Treasurer – Applies to TBI Pay service. • Escalation TBI – more than one approved user can be appointed here as a point of • Escalation Client – more than one approved user can be appointed here as a point of escalation. escalation. 3.2. 30th Aug 2022 Keith O’Sullivan Published Comply: Configuring VAT Groups Overview Purpose of this document Comply for VAT Groups. The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction on Configuring 1.1. Introduction A VAT Group is formed when a group of related companies which are under common economic ownership, register to submit VAT returns together, as a single return to the relevant Tax Authorities. In this situation, a nominated company/entity from the group is registered as the VAT Group Representative. This is the entity which is registered and responsible for submitting the returns. Please Note: The following jurisdictions do not allow VAT Groups: • Bulgaria • Lithuania • Portugal For these jurisdictions, VAT Group Details will not be displayed on the Entity > Jurisdiction Details page in Comply. Comply: Configuring VAT Groups 1.2. VAT Group Submission Types Where VAT Groups are allowed, certain jurisdictions may also have specific treatment for submissions. In Comply, we support this using VAT Group Submission Type, of which there are 3 options: 1. Consolidated, 2. Consolidated & Individual and 3. Individual. VAT Group Submission Type Consolidated Consolidated & Individual Both the VAT Group Representative and the Description The VAT Group Representative will submit only 1 return, called Consolidated, to the tax office. It will contain all the transactions for the relevant period, for the representative and the members as well. The other Members will have their individual returns, but those are called VAT Calculations, and those are not submitted to the tax office, but only used for calculations. other members are filling, calculating, and submitting their Individual returns, along with a Consolidated return, which combines the transactions of all entities in the VAT Group, for the period. Each entity from the VAT Group is filling, calculating, and submitting their individual return to the tax office. Consolidated return is not required. Individual Comply: Configuring VAT Groups 2. text: 14th Sep 2023 Keith O’Sullivan Added Jurisdiction Specifics section 1.0 1.1 Comply: How to Create a Self-Revision 1. Overview Purpose of this document a self-revision. The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction on how to create 1.1. Introduction A Self Revision allows the Comply User to either: • Create amendments to a submitted return. • Create a supplementary Return after a Return has been submitted. Please note: This functionality is only available to users who have been assigned the role of Preparer or Reviewer. Comply: How to Create a Self-Revision 1.2. Self-Revision Submission Types When creating a Self-Revision, the following options may be available: Description Revision Submission Type Amendment Create a new submission which includes all transactions details from the original return and any additional transactions which are required to be reported for this particular period. E.g. Entity has 10 transactions worth €100k of Domestic Sales which are reported in the submitted return, however 15 transactions worth €150k are actually required to be submitted. An amended return includes all transactions – the original 10 and the additional 5, and replaces the original submitted return. Create a new submission which includes only those additional which are required to be reported for this particular period. E.g. Entity has 10 transactions worth €100k of Domestic Sales which are reported in the submitted return, however 15 transactions worth €150k are actually required to be submitted. A Supplementary return includes only the additional 5 transactions, and does not replace the original return. Supplementary Comply: How to Create a Self-Revision 1.3. Self-Revision Options by Jurisdiction It is important to note that the above Self Revision options are dictated by Jurisdiction. Thus, certain jurisdictions will allow: • Amendments only. • Supplementary only. • Both ( Choice of either Amendment or Supplementary). A breakdown of this by Jurisdiction is available on the table below Jurisdictional Options Jurisdiction Armenia Australia Austria Belgium Bulgaria Croatia Czech Rep. Denmark Finland Estonia France Germany Hungary Ireland Italy Latvia Lithuania Netherlands New Zealand Norway Poland Portugal Romania Slovakia Spain Sweden Switzerland United Kingdom Type of correction return Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Supplementary Amendment Amendment Both Amendment Amendment Amendment Both Supplementary Amendment Both Amendment Both Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Amendment Comply: How to Create a Self-Revision 2. Create a Self-Revision As mentioned above, this functionality is only available to users who are assigned the role of Reviewer for a specific submitted return. 2.1. The Process 1. Open the Submitted return. Comply: How to Create a Self-Revision 2. Click the Create Self Revision button on the return details screen. The Create Self Revision Return pop up is displayed. Note: As mentioned in 1.3 above the Submission Type field will be populated by default based on the jurisdiction. The drop-down option will only be displayed for jurisdictions allow either Supplementary or Amendments. 3. Select the relevant option. Comply: How to Create a Self-Revision 4. Select the submission Deadline Date. The Deadline Date is set by default to be 1 month from the creation of the Self Revision. However the user can override this and select a new date based on their own requirements. 5. Click Open Return. A confirmation pop-up is displayed.

text: 12th Jun 2023 Keith O’Sullivan Published Comply: Processing Returns for VAT Groups Comply: Processing Returns for VAT Groups Overview Purpose of this document Returns in Comply for VAT Groups. The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction on Processing 1.1. Introduction A VAT Group is formed when a group of related companies which are under common economic ownership, register to submit VAT returns together, as a single return to the relevant Tax Authorities. In this situation, a nominated company/entity from the group is registered as the VAT Group Representative. This is the entity which is registered and responsible for submitting the returns. Please Note: The following jurisdictions do not allow VAT Groups: • Bulgaria • Lithuania • Portugal For these jurisdictions, VAT Group Details will not be displayed on the Entity > Jurisdiction Details page in Comply. Comply: Processing Returns for VAT Groups 1.2. VAT Group Submission Types Where VAT Groups are allowed, certain jurisdictions may also have specific treatment for submissions. In Comply, we support this using VAT Group Submission Type, of which there are 3 options: 1. Consolidated, 2. Consolidated & Individual and 3. Individual. VAT Group Submission Type Consolidated Consolidated & Individual Both the VAT Group Representative and the Description The VAT Group Representative will submit only 1 return, called Consolidated, to the tax office. It will contain all the transactions for the relevant period, for the representative and the members as well. The other Members will have their individual returns, but those are called VAT Calculations, and those are not submitted to the tax office, but only used for calculations. other members are filling, calculating, and submitting their Individual returns, along with a Consolidated return, which combines the transactions of all entities in the VAT Group, for the period. Each entity from the VAT Group is filling, calculating, and submitting their individual return to the tax office. Consolidated return is not required. Individual Comply: Processing Returns for VAT Groups 1.3. Submission Types by Jurisdiction These can differ by jurisdiction. Please see list below, where you can see: • Which are the countries that can form a VAT Group • Do they use the VAT Group Representative number or just they have their own VAT number as a group • The submission type.

Delegating Roles Comply can be configured to delegate an assigned users tasks to another user, i.e. in the event of a planned absence, the delegated user will receive the notifications. Example: Juan is assigned as the Data Provider for ABC Company. He has a 2 week vacation Planned, during which time he knows some of his assigned returns will have files due to be uploaded. Juan delegates his role to Carole for those 2 weeks. Carole will now receive the email notifications once the files are due, and will have access to the returns. After the 2 weeks, responsibility automatically returns to Juan. To do this: 1. Go to the Security menu. 2. Click User Details. >>Go to Next Page 3. Exclude Transaction (Control List) Following the same steps for excluding transactions, if the user excludes a transaction directly from the Control List, then the following actions are triggered: • The transaction is added to the Excluded Transactions list the relevant associated returns. • A Log is added to the Audit History of all associated returns. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of To Approve/To Submit, then these will • If any of the associated returns are on a status of Submitted, then the transaction is only excluded from the Control List, and the statuses of the VAT/VIES returns will return to To Prepare. remain on Submitted.

7.4. Exclude Transaction (Annual VAT Return) Following the same steps for excluding transactions, if the user excludes a transaction directly from the VAT/VIES Return, then the following actions are triggered: • The transaction is added to the Excluded Transactions list the relevant associated returns. • A Log is added to the Audit History of all associated returns. • The transaction is automatically removed from the Annual VAT Return. • If the associated Annual VAT return is on a status of To Approve/To Submit, then this will return to To Prepare. Comply: VAT/VIES Processing 7.5. Exclude Transactions (Amendment Self-Revision) Following the same steps for Excluding Transactions, if the user does so directly from the Self - Revision VAT/VIES Return then the following actions are triggered: • The transaction is added to the Excluded Transactions list the relevant associated returns (VAT/Annual VAT/Annual Client Listing). • A Log is added to the Audit History of all associated returns. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of To Approve/To Submit, then these will return to To Prepare. 7.6. Exclude Transactions (All Associated Returns are Submitted) If the user tries to exclude a transaction from a Quarterly VAT Return, and all the associated returns are Submitted, then the following pop-up is displayed: The user should consider opening a self-revision return or choose to disregard it. Comply: VAT/VIES Processing 8. Transactions Sent for Correction This section explores the process and steps for sending transactions for correction and includes guidance on the action triggered when related to Associated Returns. 8.1. Send a Transaction for Correction (VAT) To do this: 1. Open the VAT Return. 2. Select the transaction to be sent for correction. 3. Click Action. 4. Click Send for Correction. 5. Click Save. This Triggers the following actions: • The transaction is removed and added to the Sent for Correction list. Comply: VAT/VIES Processing • A log is added to the Audit History. 8.1.1. Associated Transactions: This also triggers the following actions in any Associated Returns, which include: • This is included in the Sent for Correction list on all associated Returns. • A log is added to the Audit History of each of the Associated Returns. Example: From associated VIES Return. • The transaction is removed from the Associated Returns. • If any of the Associated Returns are on To Approve/To Submit, then these will be returned to To Prepare. Comply: VAT/VIES Processing 8.2. Send Transaction for Correction (VIES) Following the same steps for Sending transactions for correction, if the user dos so directly from the VIES Return, then the following actions are triggered: • The transaction is added to the Sent for Correction list the relevant associated returns. • A Log is added to the Audit History of all associated returns. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of To Approve/To Submit, then these will return to To Prepare. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of Submitted, then the transaction is only sent for correction from the VIES Return, and the statuses of the VAT/Control List returns will remain on Submitted. 8.3.

8.3. Send Transaction for Correction (Control List) Following the same steps for Sending transactions for correction, if the user does so directly from the Control List Return, then the following actions are triggered: • The transaction is added to the Sent for Correction list the relevant associated returns. • A Log is added to the Audit History of all associated returns. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of To Approve/To Submit, then these will return to To Prepare. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of Submitted, then the transaction is only sent for correction from the Control List Return, and the statuses of the VAT/VIES returns will remain on Submitted. Comply: VAT/VIES Processing 8.4. Send Transaction for Correction (Annual VAT Return/Annual Client Listing) Following the same steps for Sending transactions for correction, if the user does so directly from the VAT Return, then the following actions are triggered: • The transaction is added to the Sent for Correction list the relevant associated returns (VAT/Annual VAT/Annual Client Listing). • A Log is added to the Audit History of all associated returns. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of To Approve/To Submit, then these will return to To Prepare. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of Submitted, then the transaction is only sent for correction from the VAT Return, and the statuses of the Annual VAT Return/Annual Client Listing returns will remain on Submitted. 8.5. Send Transaction for Correction (Amendment Self-Revision) Following the same steps for Sending transactions for correction, if the user does so directly from the Self -Revision VAT/VIES Return then the following actions are triggered: • The transaction is added to the Sent for Correction list the relevant associated returns (VAT/Annual VAT/Annual Client Listing). • A Log is added to the Audit History of all associated returns. • If any of the associated returns are on a status of To Approve/To Submit, then these will return to To Prepare. Comply: VAT/VIES Processing The Files Tab consists of a table of all Files uploaded to the return. This includes: 9. Files Tab • All Data Files for Upload • All Supporting Documents It also keeps a record of older deleted files. 9.1. Data Files (Source Return) The Source return is the Return to which the user uploads a Data for Return file. These files will appear here and can be viewed/downloaded/deleted directly from here. These can be sorted using the Arrows on the Status column. This will sort the column using the statuses: • Success • Pending • Deleted Comply: VAT/VIES Processing 9.2. Data Files (Associated Returns) The Associated Returns File Tab will display the uploaded Data Files for Return, but these will be Links back to the Source return. To download or delete these, the user can click the link to open the source Return. Comply: VAT/VIES Processing 9.3. Output Files If the user downloads the output file from the Source return, this will display all transactions. 9.3.1. Source Return 9.3.2. Associated Return If, however the user is on the VIES return, and there are VIES related transaction (EUP/EUS/TRS), then only these transactions will be displayed in the downloaded Output file.

Associated Return If, however the user is on the VIES return, and there are VIES related transaction (EUP/EUS/TRS), then only these transactions will be displayed in the downloaded Output file. Comply: VAT/VIES Processing 10. Email Alerts and Notifications Email notifications are automatically sent to the Preparer anytime the status of a Return/Associated Return is set back to To Prepare. This is an automated process triggered by Editing, Adding, Excluding or Sending a transaction where a Return/Associated Return is on To Review/To Approve/To Submit. Example: Comply: VAT/VIES Processing 11. Return Review & XML The user once happy with all Transactions and associated returns, they can review the Return Boxes and the generated return files by visiting the Return Review Screen. The Return can be processed through To Approve > To Submit. 12. Submit Finally, if all is in good order and the user is happy with the return. The they can click Submit. (For Digital Submission, this is only available in Germany and the UK). For the majority of Jurisdiction, the user can then download the return Submission file from the Return Review Tab, and upload to the relevant Tax Authority portal.

26th Sept 2023 Keith O’Sullivan Added Previous Return Deviations 1.0 1.1 Purpose of this document processing a Return in Comply. The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction on the lifecycle of Comply processes a return through the following steps/processes which are in turn assigned to a specific user: Data Provider This role is assigned to a System user, which allows clients to use an API to upload relevant return data. Data Preparer This requires the user to review and prepare the uploaded data file. Reviewer good order. This requires the user to review the prepared data to ensure it is in Approver This requires the user to review the prepared data to ensure it is in good order and approve it ready for Submission. Submitter This requires the user to review the prepared data to ensure it is in good order and submit it to the relevant TAX office. 1. Notifications The platform is configurable to allow the users receive notifications by email. These notifications are a key part of the process for each user role and identify when a task assigned E.g. When configured, the data provider will receive a notification by email, when data for a to you requires action. specific return is due. Notes: each task. • Notifications are linked to the scheduler, so will be triggered by the date assigned for • It is important that you have configured these notifications first, so that when tasks assigned to you become due, you will be made aware and can action them on time. • Notifications are sent overnight. • Regardless of the frequency a user has chosen, notifications are only sent once. • If you select Daily notifications, you will only receive one if you have assigned tasks due. deadline. What does the user receive? The user will only receive notifications if: • The action is “Due Now”. This means action is required within the next 3 days. • The action is required and is “Overdue”. This means, the action is late (based on the preconfigured deadlines) and puts the return at risk of missing the statutory submission Only the person assigned the relevant role, will receive these notifications. I.e. Only the Preparer will receive notification for returns which have been moved to a status of “To Prepare” and action is due within 3 days. 1.1. Configure User Notifications Notifications are a key part of the process for each user role. These identify when a task assigned to you requires action. It is important that you have configured the notifications, so that when tasks assigned to you become due, you will be made aware and can action them on time. Please note: If you do not complete this step, you will not receive notifications when tasks assigned to you are due. You will need to review the Returns menu more frequently. The following Steps are required to successfully complete this process: 1. Login to Comply. 2. Click Security on the Menu. 3. Click User Details on the sub-menu. 4. Locate the Settings options. 5. Click the Pen icon to enable edit mode. 6. Click the Notification Preferences drop-down option. 7. Select a relevant notification type, from the following options: • Once a Day • Once every two days • Once every three days • Once a week • Once a month • No notifications 1.2.

7. Select a relevant notification type, from the following options: • Once a Day • Once every two days • Once every three days • Once a week • Once a month • No notifications 1.2. Viewing Email Notifications Example 1: Once a return is due, the Data Provider will receive a notification identifying that the data file is due to be uploaded and will display a status of Data Due. Example 2: Once a data provider uploads the data file, the preparer receives a notification to say they have a return assigned to them, which has a task due. The status will say To Prepare. Email Notification The user will receive a notification email to their inbox. Below as a sample of an email reminder: Note: If the user is responsible for multiple roles and multiple returns, the reminder may be combined and grouped appropriately in the email. The user is advised to login to Comply to take the necessary actions. 2. Email Alerts Unlike standard notifications outlined in section 1 above, Email Alerts are not linked to the scheduler but are instead triggered by specific actions due or by specific actions which have been taken. Note: scheduler. These alerts are sent in addition to the standard notifications sent which are linked to the • Standard Notifications linked to the scheduler are only sent if notifications have been configured (as in page 6 above). • Email Alerts are sent by default, regardless of whether notifications have been configured. 2.1. Action Required: Return Data-Due Tomorrow The following E-mail is sent to the Data Provider at 7am local time on the working day before the data is due. This alerts the Data Provider that the data is due on the next working day and that they should login and upload the relevant data file. E.g. The Data is due on Monday 30th Sept, then the Data Provider will receive the email at 7am on Friday 27th Sept. Key Notes: return. • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Data-Due Tomorrow”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. 2.2. Action Required: Return Data Upload – Deadline Passed The following E-mail is sent to the Data Provider at 7am on the next working day after the Data Upload was due. This alerts the Data Provider that action is required immediately as the return is at risk of being filed late. The user should log on to Comply and upload the data file. E.g. The Data Upload was due on Friday Sept 1st but as the file was not uploaded, the Data Provider will receive an email at 7am on Monday 4th Sept. A • The Subject is “Action Required: Return Data Upload – Deadline Passed”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. Key Notes: return. 2.3.

Key Notes: return. 2.3. Action Required: Return Ready for Approval The following E-mail is sent to the Approver immediately once a return had been Sent to Approve by the Reviewer. This alerts the approver that a return they are assigned has been reviewed and is ready to Approve. They should now login to Comply and Approve (or Reject if E.g. The Reviewer clicks the Send for Approval button, this triggers an immediate automatic required) the return. Email to the Approver Key Notes: • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Ready for Approval”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. return. 2.4. Action Required: Return Successfully Submitted. Arrange Payment Where Required. The following E-mail is sent to the Approver and/or Treasurer (if they are not the same person, then it will be sent to both) immediately once a return had been Submitted. This alerts the Approver and/or Treasurer that a return they are assigned has been Submitted and is ready for payment. They should now arrange payment. E.g. The Approver clicks the Submit button, this triggers an immediate automatic Email to the Approver and/or Treasurer Key Notes: where required”. • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Successfully Submitted. Arrange payment • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. return. 2.5. Action Required: Return Reverted back to “To Prepare” The following E-mail is sent to the Preparer immediately once the status of a return has reverted back to “To Prepare”. This alerts the Preparer that: • The return has changed back to “To Prepare”. • The Submission Deadline for that return. • The return could be at risk of being submitted late. E.g. If prior to submission, the return is rejected, this triggers an immediate automatic Email to the Preparer. Please Note: A return can be reverted back to “To Prepare” from the following statuses: • From “To Review” to “To Prepare” • From “To Approve” to “To Prepare” • From “To Submit” to “To Prepare” Key Notes: return. • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Reverted from [-Status-] back to ”To Prepare”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. 2.5.1. From “To Review” to “To Prepare” 2.5.2. From “To Approve” to “To Prepare” 2.5.3.

2.5.1. From “To Review” to “To Prepare” 2.5.2. From “To Approve” to “To Prepare” 2.5.3. From “To Submit” to “ To Prepare” 2.6. Action Required: Return Approval – Deadline Passed The following E-mail is sent to the Data Provider at 7am local time on the working day after the return is due to be approved. This alerts the Approver that the return is overdue and that the return is at risk of being filed late if immediate action is not taken. The user should log in and take the appropriate action E.g. The approval was due on Monday 30th Sept, then the approver will receive the email at 7am on Tuesday 1st Oct (or nearest working day). • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Approval – Deadline Passed”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant Key Notes: return. • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. 3. Delegating Roles Comply can be configured to delegate an assigned users tasks to another user, i.e. in the event of a planned absence, the delegated user will receive the notifications. Example: Juan is assigned as the Data Provider for ABC Company. He has a 2 week vacation Planned, during which time he knows some of his assigned returns will have files due to be uploaded. Juan delegates his role to Carole for those 2 weeks. Carole will now receive the email notifications once the files are due, and will have access to the returns. After the 2 weeks, responsibility automatically returns to Juan. To do this: 1. Go to the Security menu. 2. Click User Details. >>Go to Next Page 3. In the Report Role section, click the Pencil Icon beside the role you wish to delegate. 4. Click the green + button to add a name. 5. Add a name (select from a drop-down) and Select a date range (From and To). 6. Click Apply. This automatically returns to the original user after the date range is complete. 4. Escalation Triggers Comply can also be configured to notify a specific user when certain tasks (assigned to others) are overdue. E.g. If the Data Provider has not uploaded the file on time, a notification can be triggered to escalate it to a designated person who can investigate the issue. Please note: This functionality only works when the specific role of Escalation Manager has been assigned (this is configured by an admin user). Security > User Details To configure the Escalation Trigger (if you are an Escalation Manager): 1. Go to Security. 2. Click User Details. 3. Go to Settings. 4. Click the icon, to open the edit mode. 5. Go to Escalation Trigger. 7. Click Save. 6. Enter the number of days after which a task is overdue, is escalated to you. 5.

4. Click the icon, to open the edit mode. 5. Go to Escalation Trigger. 7. Click Save. 6. Enter the number of days after which a task is overdue, is escalated to you. 5. Processing a Return (API Users) For clients using API’s for data upload, it is key that during onboarding the Data Provider role is assigned to System Bot (as opposed to a physical user). This is generally configured during onboarding or by an Admin User. Security > User Roles All relevant client data will be uploaded via the API and pushed through preconfigured mapping and validation. The Return details will be made available to the Preparer and will have a status of To Prepare. 5.1. Return Status a status of To Prepare. Clients using API to upload return data will only manually process returns in Comply which have Data Due Return Status Displayed Prior to first transaction Data Due pushed via API After first transaction To Prepare pushed via API 5.1.1. Before first transaction is pushed via API 5.1.2. After first transaction is pushed via API 6. Preparer Based on the scheduled due date for the To Prepare step , the assigned preparer will receive an email notification (based on how they have configured their notification preferences). The following steps can now be used to prepare the return. Open the return in Comply. The data upload has been successful and the data has been run through the Comply data transformation and rules engine. The transformed file is available now for review and preparation. 6.1. Data Validation. Click the Data Validation Tab. This displays a list of the rules and validation checks. If any of these display errors, the preparer needs to assess and make the necessary changes where possible. To make changes or to fix any errors: 1. Click on the relevant row on which the error has been displayed. This will display the rule, where the validation has failed. 2. Use the scroll bar to locate the highlighted section, this will display the validation error. In this particular example, the error relates to the VAT Rate. The wrong VAT Rate was uploaded as part of the Data File. The VAT Rate for Germany is 19, so this will need to be amended by the data preparer. 3. Select the errors you wish to edit. 4. Click Edit. 5. Change the values in the highlighted fields to the correct VAT Rate Value. 6. Click Save. continue. 7. Click the blue Submit button at the bottom of the screen to submit the changes and In this case, all the errors were in fact related to the incorrect VAT Rate, so by changing it in error, has fixed all the other related errors. We can see that all 133 validation checks have now been processed successfully. He user can now move onto the next step. 6.2. Transactions. Click the Transactions tab. The data preparer, should review the transactions here, to confirm they are in good order. Comply includes built in functionality to allow the user filter or customise how they wish the data to be displayed on this screen. 1. Display Transactions by: These colour coded buttons allow the user display transactions by: • Transactions Added • Transactions Modified • Transactions sent for Correction • Transactions Excluded 2. Download Transactions This allows the user to download the full list of transactions in the table displayed 3.

Download Transactions This allows the user to download the full list of transactions in the table displayed 3. Add Transactions This allows the user to manually add transaction perhaps not included in the upload. The user can manually complete the required fields and upload any relevant files. 4. Edit Columns This allows the user to edit the view to display specific relevant columns and data. 5. Filer the displayed data. The user can also filter the data to display on a subset of the transactions. 6.2.1. Edit a transaction If required during review, the preparer can amend transactions at this stage. To do this: 1. Select the relevant transaction to amend (Click the check box). 2. Click the Edit button. 3. Complete/update the relevant available fields. 4. To save the changes, simply untick the box. 6.2.2. Transaction Actions any of these the user can: The user can also perform specific actions in relation to these transactions. Again, to perform 1. Select the relevant transaction to amend (Click the check box). 2. Click the Action button. 3. Select the required Action. Send for Correction Upon review, the user can chose to send the transaction back to be corrected. In this case the user must select a reason from the drop down menu and click Save. This does not impact the ability to process this return, but once corrected, the transaction will be added to a later return. Exclude from Return Upon review, the user can chose for the transaction back to be excluded from this return. In this case the user must select a reason from the drop down menu and click Save. This does not impact the ability to process this return and the transaction will not be added to any later return. Move to a Different Return chose to move it. If the user reviews and identifies a transaction which does not belong in this return, they can To do this, the user must select the reason from the drop down menu and also select the relevant return for it to be moved to. That complete the Transactions section. 6.3. Return Validation Click the Return Validation tab. The Data Preparer should review the validation checks for errors or warnings. They should also check and review the Variance Analysis. Here, Comply provides built in Analytics tools to help the preparer in identifying trends, variances and data analysis. You can also view Analytics from the main menu. From here the data preparer can review the return in detail in preparation for sending for review. 6.4. Return Review Click the Return Review tab. Here they can: • View/Amend Numerical Boxes • View/Amend Non-Numerical Boxes • View and download the Return in its downloadable formats • Change the review from English to local Language 6.4.1. Numerical Boxes for accuracy and amended if required. Here the user can review the numerical boxes and their values. These again should be reviewed To amend a box: 1. Click the pencil Icon . 2. Click Add. 3. Add the change to the available field in the new adjustment row. 4. Add a relevant comment and add any relevant supporting files (if required). 5. Click Save. 6.4.2. Return Review Deviations The Numerical Boxes now include relevant previous period data.

4. Add a relevant comment and add any relevant supporting files (if required). 5. Click Save. 6.4.2. Return Review Deviations The Numerical Boxes now include relevant previous period data. This is used as a visual comparison with previous periods which allows the user to make informed decisions relating to This includes the following new columns which have been added to the Numerical Boxes: the current return. • Previous Period • Deviations • Previous Year • Attachments Columns month. box). • Previous Period – this displays the values from the previous return. • Deviations – this displays deviations of the current month compared with the previous • Previous Year – this displays the values from the same period of the previous year • Attachments – the ability to attach supporting files which help provide clarity on the deviations (PDF, Word, Xls, Xlxs , JPEG ,PNG or copies of emails on a numerical return Column Headers The user can hover over each column header for more information on what the column displays: This column displays the value from the Submitted Value from the previous return. Previous Period Current Return Previous Return (5686) Deviations The Deviations column displays a % fluctuation (Positive/Negative) of the current month compared to the previous month. It is also colour coded. Description Logic Green Red Where the deviation is below 50%, then that value is shown in green. Where the deviation is equal to/above 50%, then that value is shown in red. Up Arrow If the percentage is positive, then the value displays a Up Arrow Icon. Down Arrow If the percentage is negative, then the value displays a Down Arrow Icon. This Colum displays the Submitted Values from the same period, but from the previous year. E.g. The submitted values figure from Jan 2022 are populated in the Previous Year field for the Previous Year Jan 2023 return. Attachments This allows the user to add/view supporting files to add clarity around the deviation. Please note: A max limit of 10 MB is placed on file uploads. 6.4.3. Non-Numerical Boxes Here the user can review the non-numerical boxes and their values. These again should be reviewed for accuracy and amended if required. To amend a box: 1. Click the pencil Icon . 2. Add/Amend the information in the editable field. 3. Click the Pencil icon again to save the changes. made. Please Note: The Orange Info button, allows the user to see an Audit Trail of amendments 6.4.4. View Return 1. Click View Return. The user can also view the return in its available formats. To do this: The return documents will be displayed as clickable links in each format: 2. Click a link to open the review. This will download the relevant file. Sample PDF Return. 6.4.5. Change the Return to Local Language Comply produces the return by default in English, however the user can chose to change this to local language if required. To do this chose Local Language using the toggle as seen below. That completes the Data Preparers required actions. If the user is happy with the review and preparation, then they should click Send For Review. 6.5. Manually Add a New Return To add a new return: 1. Go to the All Returns screen. 2. Click the Add Line button. 3. Complete the relevant mandatory fields on the Add Return Pop-Up.

6.5. Manually Add a New Return To add a new return: 1. Go to the All Returns screen. 2. Click the Add Line button. 3. Complete the relevant mandatory fields on the Add Return Pop-Up. This includes: a. Entity Code b. Jurisdiction c. Frequency d. Return Type Frequency). e. Return Start and End Dates (End date will auto populate based on Return 4. Click Submit. 7. Audit History Using the Audit History button at any stage during the lifecycle of a return, the user can review an audit trail of all changes made to that return. Navigation: • Open a Return • Click the Audit History button. 1. The Audit History screen can be filtered to display: • All History Logs – all changes made to the return across all Event Groups. • Return Logs only – changes made at return level including statuses. • Transaction Logs Only – changes made at transactional level only. E.g. 1 Transactional Level: A user makes a change to the posting date of a transaction. E.g. 2 Return Level: the lifecycle of the return. Return Status change. The Return is moved from one status to another during 2. Download Logs – here the user can download the logs to be reviewed/stored offline. Note: The file downloaded will display the logs based on how the screen has been filtered (if filters are applied). 3. Audit History display – This displays the log in table form including each change/update by: • Date & Time • Event Group • Event From • Event To • User Name • Comments – This will display any comment added at the time of the change. • Type- Transaction/Return • ID 8. Reviewer The Reviewer (again if they have configured their notifications), will receive the notification email that they have a return to action. And the return will be displayed in the Assigned to Me section of their returns screen in Comply. The job of the reviewer is to open and review the data in each of the following tabs to ensure the preparer has not missed anything and to ensure it is in good order before sending for Approval: Data Validation The reviewer will check for any errors where required. Transactions The Reviewer will check the transaction data for any missing or errors in the data. Next Page Return Validation Again here, the Reviewer is just checking the work completed by the Preparer, ensuring the validation of the data against the rules is complete and in good order. Return Review approval. The Reviewer here can review the final values and view the return files before sending for Please note, if there are any issues found at this stage the user can Reject the return, in which case it reverts back to a Status of To Prepare and is returned to the Preparer for review. 8.1. Send for Approval If all is in good order, then the Reviewer simply clicks the Send for Approval button. This changes the status to To Approve. Based on the schedule due date for the Approval step, a notification email is sent to the Approver that there is a return for them to action. Please note: The user can leave a comment (If there is key information for the Approver to know). That completes the Reviewer process. 9. Approver Approving the return. The Approver essentially repeats the same data checks as the Reviewer before rejecting or Once reviewed, the user clicks Approve. This changes the status automatically to To Submit.

That completes the Reviewer process. 9. Approver Approving the return. The Approver essentially repeats the same data checks as the Reviewer before rejecting or Once reviewed, the user clicks Approve. This changes the status automatically to To Submit. That completes the Approver process and triggers the notification mail to be sent to the Submitter. 10. Submitter The Submitter will either log in directly to Comply or via a notification email advising that the return has been approved in is ready to be submitted. Here the Submitter has the option to review the return details again or simply Submit the return. To do this, the user simply: 1. Open the Return. 2. Click the Return Review tab. 3. Click the Submit button. (if they are happy with the data). 4. This changes the status of the return to “Submitting”. Once this changes to Submitted, this automatically triggers an immediate Email Alert to the Approver and/or Treasurer advising the return has been successfully submitted and they should make payment.
