text: 26th July 2022 Keith O’Sullivan Published 19th Sep 2022 Keith O’Sullivan Added Email Alerts - Published 26th Sept 2023 Keith O’Sullivan Previous Return Deviations 1.0 1.1 1.2 Comply: Returns Processing Overview Purpose of this document The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction for users who are assigned the role of Data Provider. This role is usually assigned to client users to upload the relevant data file(s) for the specific return period. Comply processes a return through the following steps/processes which are in turn assigned to a specific user: Data Provider This requires the user to upload the return data file to Comply. Data Preparer This requires the user to review and prepare the uploaded data file. Reviewer good order. This requires the user to review the prepared data to ensure it is in Approver This requires the user to review the prepared data to ensure it is in good order and approve it ready for Submission. Submitter This requires the user to review the prepared data to ensure it is in good order and submit it to the relevant TAX office. Comply: Returns Processing During set up, users will be assigned their individual roles. Users can view their assigned roles by navigating to the Security menu: Security > User Details In this example, you can see that the user has actually been assigned to each role across the return process. However, in most cases, client users will usually see their own role as either Data Provider or Data Approver. Comply: Returns Processing 1. Notifications The platform is configurable to allow the users receive notifications by email. These notifications are a key part of the process for each user role and identify when a task assigned E.g. When configured, the data provider will receive a notification by email, when data for a to you requires action. specific return is due. Notes: each task. • Notifications are linked to the scheduler, so will be triggered by the date assigned for • It is important that you have configured these notifications first, so that when tasks assigned to you become due, you will be made aware and can action them on time. • Notifications are sent overnight. • Regardless of the frequency a user has chosen, notifications are only sent once. • If you select Daily notifications, you will only receive one if you have assigned tasks due. deadline. What does the user receive? The user will only receive notifications if: • The action is “Due Now”. This means action is required within the next 3 days. • The action is required and is “Overdue”. This means, the action is late (based on the preconfigured deadlines) and puts the return at risk of missing the statutory submission Only the person assigned the relevant role, will receive these notifications. I.e. Only the Preparer will receive notification for returns which have been moved to a status of “To Prepare” and action is due within 3 days. Comply: Returns Processing 1.1. Configure User Notifications Notifications are a key part of the process for each user role. These identify when a task assigned to you requires action. It is important that you have configured the notifications, so that when tasks assigned to you become due, you will be made aware and can action them on time. Please note: If you do not complete this step, you will not receive notifications when tasks assigned to you are due.

Please note: If you do not complete this step, you will not receive notifications when tasks assigned to you are due. You will need to review the Returns menu more frequently. The following Steps are required to successfully complete this process: 1. Login to Comply. 2. Click Security on the Menu. 3. Click User Details on the sub-menu. 4. Locate the Settings options. Comply: Returns Processing 5. Click the Pen icon to enable edit mode. 6. Click the Notification Preferences drop-down option. 7. Select a relevant notification type, from the following options: • Once a Day • Once every two days • Once every three days • Once a week • Once a month • No notifications Comply: Returns Processing 1.2. Viewing Email Notifications Example 1: Once a return is due, the Data Provider will receive a notification identifying that the data file is due to be uploaded and will display a status of Data Due. Example 2: Once a data provider uploads the data file, the preparer receives a notification to say they have a return assigned to them, which has a task due. The status will say To Prepare. Email Notification The user will receive a notification email to their inbox. Below as a sample of an email reminder: Note: If the user is responsible for multiple roles and multiple returns, the reminder may be combined and grouped appropriately in the email. The user is advised to login to Comply to take the necessary actions. Comply: Returns Processing 2. Email Alerts Unlike standard notifications outlined in section 1 above, Email Alerts are not linked to the scheduler but are instead triggered by specific actions due or by specific actions which have been taken. Note: scheduler. These alerts are sent in addition to the standard notifications sent which are linked to the • Standard Notifications linked to the scheduler are only sent if notifications have been configured (as in page 6 above). • Email Alerts are sent by default, regardless of whether notifications have been configured. Comply: Returns Processing 2.1. Action Required: Return Data-Due Tomorrow The following E-mail is sent to the Data Provider at 7am local time on the working day before the data is due. This alerts the Data Provider that the data is due on the next working day and that they should login and upload the relevant data file. E.g. The Data is due on Monday 30th Sept, then the Data Provider will receive the email at 7am on Friday 27th Sept. Key Notes: return. • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Data-Due Tomorrow”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. Comply: Returns Processing 2.2. Action Required: Return Data Upload – Deadline Passed The following E-mail is sent to the Data Provider at 7am on the next working day after the Data Upload was due. This alerts the Data Provider that action is required immediately as the return is at risk of being filed late. The user should log on to Comply and upload the data file. E.g.

This alerts the Data Provider that action is required immediately as the return is at risk of being filed late. The user should log on to Comply and upload the data file. E.g. The Data Upload was due on Friday Sept 1st but as the file was not uploaded, the Data Provider will receive an email at 7am on Monday 4th Sept. A • The Subject is “Action Required: Return Data Upload – Deadline Passed”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. Key Notes: return. Comply: Returns Processing 2.3. Action Required: Return Ready for Approval The following E-mail is sent to the Approver immediately once a return had been Sent to Approve by the Reviewer. This alerts the approver that a return they are assigned has been reviewed and is ready to Approve. They should now login to Comply and Approve (or Reject if E.g. The Reviewer clicks the Send for Approval button, this triggers an immediate automatic required) the return. Email to the Approver Key Notes: • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Ready for Approval”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. return. Comply: Returns Processing 2.4. Action Required: Return Successfully Submitted. Arrange Payment Where Required. The following E-mail is sent to the Approver and/or Treasurer (if they are not the same person, then it will be sent to both) immediately once a return had been Submitted. This alerts the Approver and/or Treasurer that a return they are assigned has been Submitted and is ready for payment. They should now arrange payment. E.g. The Approver clicks the Submit button, this triggers an immediate automatic Email to the Approver and/or Treasurer Key Notes: where required”. • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Successfully Submitted. Arrange payment • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. return. Comply: Returns Processing 2.5. Action Required: Return Reverted back to “To Prepare” The following E-mail is sent to the Preparer immediately once the status of a return has reverted back to “To Prepare”. This alerts the Preparer that: • The return has changed back to “To Prepare”. • The Submission Deadline for that return. • The return could be at risk of being submitted late. E.g. If prior to submission, the return is rejected, this triggers an immediate automatic Email to the Preparer.

E.g. If prior to submission, the return is rejected, this triggers an immediate automatic Email to the Preparer. Please Note: A return can be reverted back to “To Prepare” from the following statuses: • From “To Review” to “To Prepare” • From “To Approve” to “To Prepare” • From “To Submit” to “To Prepare” Key Notes: return. • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Reverted from [-Status-] back to ”To Prepare”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. From “To Submit” to “ To Prepare” Comply: Returns Processing 2.6. Action Required: Return Approval – Deadline Passed The following E-mail is sent to the Data Provider at 7am local time on the working day after the return is due to be approved. This alerts the Approver that the return is overdue and that the return is at risk of being filed late if immediate action is not taken. The user should log in and take the appropriate action E.g. The approval was due on Monday 30th Sept, then the approver will receive the email at 7am on Tuesday 1st Oct (or nearest working day). • The Subject is “Action Required – Return Approval – Deadline Passed”. • The E-mail is a “DO NOT RESPOND” notification. • The E-mail contains a link back to the Return in Comply – on clicking the link, the user will be asked to Authenticate (Sign in) and will automatically be brought to the relevant Key Notes: return. • The E-mail contains a link (In the Signature) which links back to the Support Desk. Comply: Returns Processing 3. Delegating Roles Comply can be configured to delegate an assigned users tasks to another user, i.e. in the event of a planned absence, the delegated user will receive the notifications. Example: Juan is assigned as the Data Provider for ABC Company. He has a 2 week vacation Planned, during which time he knows some of his assigned returns will have files due to be uploaded. Juan delegates his role to Carole for those 2 weeks. Carole will now receive the email notifications once the files are due, and will have access to the returns. After the 2 weeks, responsibility automatically returns to Juan. To do this: 1. Go to the Security menu. 2. Click User Details. >>Go to Next Page Comply: Returns Processing 3. In the Report Role section, click the Pencil Icon beside the role you wish to delegate. 4. Click the green + button to add a name. Comply: Returns Processing 5. Add a name (select from a drop-down) and Select a date range (From and To). 6. Click Apply. This automatically returns to the original user after the date range is complete.

Comply: Returns Processing 5. Add a name (select from a drop-down) and Select a date range (From and To). 6. Click Apply. This automatically returns to the original user after the date range is complete. Comply: Returns Processing 4. Escalation Triggers Comply can also be configured to notify a specific user when certain tasks (assigned to others) are overdue. E.g. If the Data Provider has not uploaded the file on time, a notification can be triggered to escalate it to a designated person who can investigate the issue. Please note: This functionality only works when the specific role of Escalation Manager has been assigned (this is configured by an admin user). Security > User Details To configure the Escalation Trigger (if you are an Escalation Manager): 1. Go to Security. 2. Click User Details. 3. Go to Settings. Comply: Returns Processing 4. Click the icon, to open the edit mode. 5. Go to Escalation Trigger. 7. Click Save. 6. Enter the number of days after which a task is overdue, is escalated to you. Comply: Returns Processing 5. Data Provider 5.1. Upload the Data File 1. Navigate to the Returns Menu. Once the data provider receives notification that the return is due, they should login to Comply. 2. By default, the returns displayed will be all returns those assigned to you. Set a data range filter if you wish to display returns for a specific period only. Comply: Returns Processing 3. Click the return you wish to upload a data file for. For this example, I (as the Data Provider) am required to upload a date for the return ID 27. It is currently displaying as Data Due, it is for the Return Period April 2022, with a Return Deadline of 09/06/2022. This opens the Return details screen. Comply: Returns Processing The details pane can be expanded by clicking the green arrow. This provides the user with additional return specific information. The user can also review the Return Timeline. This provides the user a look at the overall steps required to be completed and the deadlines for each one. Comply: Returns Processing 4. Upload the Data File. To select the file from its current location the user can: Note: Password protected files cannot be uploaded. • Drag and Drop a file • Click the Choose File button. 5. From the drop-down menu, select Data File for Return. Comply: Returns Processing Note: Comply allows the user the ability to upload other supporting documentation if required. This is optional. 5.1.1. Upload a Supporting Doc Uploading additional files which provide supporting information is possible, but this information is not used in the calculation or generation of the return. To do this: 1. In the files tab, click to Upload or Drag and Drop a file to add. 2. Select Supporting Document from the drop-down menu Depending on the file type, Supporting Document may be the only option. Comply: Returns Processing 6. Once the Data File for Return/Supporting Document is attached, click Upload. The file is then uploaded and goes through a data transformation process, which runs the data against the comply rules engine to ensure the data is in good order to run through Comply. Once complete, the return status changes to To Prepare.

The file is then uploaded and goes through a data transformation process, which runs the data against the comply rules engine to ensure the data is in good order to run through Comply. Once complete, the return status changes to To Prepare. Comply: Returns Processing Based on the assigned due date for the Data Preparation step, a notification is sent to the Data Preparer (providing they have configured their notifications settings), and the Return will now be visible for them in their Returns section once they login. That completes the process for the Data Provider. The Data Preparer will now review the data and complete their process to ensure the data is correct and in good order, at which point they will send it to the Reviewer, who will review it and send for the clients approval before the actual submission. 5.2. Upload a NIL Return Where required, the client may have a situation, where it necessary to upload a NIL return. This is accommodated in Comply by completing the following steps: 1. The Data Provider opens the required Return. 2. Click the green down arrow on the Return. Go to next page Comply: Returns Processing 3. Turn on the “Is Nil Return” switch. 4. This automatically moves the status to To Prepare as there is no file to upload. 5. The automatic notification is sent to the preparer (based on the scheduled due date for preparation). Comply: Returns Processing 6. Preparer Based on the scheduled due date for the To Prepare step , the assigned preparer will receive an email notification (based on how they have configured their notification preferences). The following steps can now be used to prepare the return. Open the return in Comply. Comply: Returns Processing The data upload has been successful and the data has been run through the Comply data transformation and rules engine. The transformed file is available now for review and preparation. Comply: Returns Processing 6.1. Data Validation. Click the Data Validation Tab. This displays a list of the rules and validation checks. If any of these display errors, the preparer needs to assess and make the necessary changes where possible. To make changes or to fix any errors: 1. Click on the relevant row on which the error has been displayed. This will display the rule, where the validation has failed. 2. Use the scroll bar to locate the highlighted section, this will display the validation error. Comply: Returns Processing In this particular example, the error relates to the VAT Rate. The wrong VAT Rate was uploaded as part of the Data File. The VAT Rate for Germany is 19, so this will need to be amended by the data preparer. 3. Select the errors you wish to edit. 4. Click Edit. Comply: Returns Processing 5. Change the values in the highlighted fields to the correct VAT Rate Value. 6. Click Save. continue. 7. Click the blue Submit button at the bottom of the screen to submit the changes and In this case, all the errors were in fact related to the incorrect VAT Rate, so by changing it in error, has fixed all the other related errors. We can see that all 133 validation checks have now been processed successfully. He user can now move onto the next step. Comply: Returns Processing 6.2. Transactions. Click the Transactions tab. The data preparer, should review the transactions here, to confirm they are in good order.

He user can now move onto the next step. Comply: Returns Processing 6.2. Transactions. Click the Transactions tab. The data preparer, should review the transactions here, to confirm they are in good order. Comply includes built in functionality to allow the user filter or customise how they wish the data to be displayed on this screen. Comply: Returns Processing 1. Display Transactions by: These colour coded buttons allow the user display transactions by: • Transactions Added • Transactions Modified • Transactions sent for Correction • Transactions Excluded 2. Download Transactions This allows the user to download the full list of transactions in the table displayed 3. Add Transactions This allows the user to manually add transaction perhaps not included in the upload. The user can manually complete the required fields and upload any relevant files. The user can also filter the data to display on a subset of the transactions. Comply: Returns Processing 6.2.1. Edit a transaction If required during review, the preparer can amend transactions at this stage. To do this: 1. Select the relevant transaction to amend (Click the check box). 2. Click the Edit button. 3. Complete/update the relevant available fields. 4. To save the changes, simply untick the box. 6.2.2. Transaction Actions any of these the user can: The user can also perform specific actions in relation to these transactions. Again, to perform 1. Select the relevant transaction to amend (Click the check box). 2. Click the Action button. 3. Select the required Action. Comply: Returns Processing Send for Correction Upon review, the user can chose to send the transaction back to be corrected. In this case the user must select a reason from the drop down menu and click Save. This does not impact the ability to process this return, but once corrected, the transaction will be added to a later return. Exclude from Return Upon review, the user can chose for the transaction back to be excluded from this return. In this case the user must select a reason from the drop down menu and click Save. This does not impact the ability to process this return and the transaction will not be added to any later return. Comply: Returns Processing Move to a Different Return chose to move it. If the user reviews and identifies a transaction which does not belong in this return, they can To do this, the user must select the reason from the drop down menu and also select the relevant return for it to be moved to. That complete the Transactions section. Comply: Returns Processing 6.3. Return Validation Click the Return Validation tab. The Data Preparer should review the validation checks for errors or warnings. They should also check and review the Variance Analysis. Here, Comply provides built in Analytics tools to help the preparer in identifying trends, variances and data analysis. You can also view Analytics from the main menu. From here the data preparer can review the return in detail in preparation for sending for review. Comply: Returns Processing 6.4. Return Review Click the Return Review tab.

You can also view Analytics from the main menu. From here the data preparer can review the return in detail in preparation for sending for review. Comply: Returns Processing 6.4. Return Review Click the Return Review tab. Here they can: • View/Amend Numerical Boxes • View/Amend Non-Numerical Boxes • View and download the Return in its downloadable formats • Change the review from English to local Language 6.4.1. Numerical Boxes for accuracy and amended if required. Here the user can review the numerical boxes and their values. These again should be reviewed To amend a box: 1. Click the pencil Icon . 2. Click Add. Comply: Returns Processing 3. Add the change to the available field in the new adjustment row. 4. Add a relevant comment and add any relevant supporting files (if required). 5. Click Save. Comply: Returns Processing 6.4.2. Return Review Deviations The Numerical Boxes now include relevant previous period data. This is used as a visual comparison with previous periods which allows the user to make informed decisions relating to This includes the following new columns which have been added to the Numerical Boxes: the current return. • Previous Period • Deviations • Previous Year • Attachments Columns month. box). • Previous Period – this displays the values from the previous return. • Deviations – this displays deviations of the current month compared with the previous • Previous Year – this displays the values from the same period of the previous year • Attachments – the ability to attach supporting files which help provide clarity on the deviations (PDF, Word, Xls, Xlxs , JPEG ,PNG or copies of emails on a numerical return Comply: Returns Processing Column Headers The user can hover over each column header for more information on what the column displays: This column displays the value from the Submitted Value from the previous return. Comply: Returns Processing 6.4.3. Non-Numerical Boxes Here the user can review the non-numerical boxes and their values. These again should be reviewed for accuracy and amended if required. To amend a box: 1. Click the pencil Icon . 2. Add/Amend the information in the editable field. 3. Click the Pencil icon again to save the changes. made.

The user can also view the return in its available formats. To do this: The return documents will be displayed as clickable links in each format: 2. Click a link to open the review. This will download the relevant file. Comply: Returns Processing Sample PDF Return. Comply: Returns Processing 6.4.5. Change the Return to Local Language Comply produces the return by default in English, however the user can chose to change this to local language if required. To do this chose Local Language using the toggle as seen below. That completes the Data Preparers required actions. If the user is happy with the review and preparation, then they should click Send For Review. Comply: Returns Processing 6.5. Manually Add a New Return To add a new return: 1. Go to the All Returns screen. 2. Click the Add Line button. 3. Complete the relevant mandatory fields on the Add Return Pop-Up. This includes: a. Entity Code b. Jurisdiction c. Frequency d. Return Type Frequency). e. Return Start and End Dates (End date will auto populate based on Return 4. Click Submit. Comply: Returns Processing 7. Audit History Using the Audit History button at any stage during the lifecycle of a return, the user can review an audit trail of all changes made to that return. Navigation: • Open a Return • Click the Audit History button. 1. The Audit History screen can be filtered to display: • All History Logs – all changes made to the return across all Event Groups. • Return Logs only – changes made at return level including statuses. • Transaction Logs Only – changes made at transactional level only. Comply: Returns Processing E.g. 1 Transactional Level: A user makes a change to the posting date of a transaction. E.g. 2 Return Level: the lifecycle of the return. Return Status change. The Return is moved from one status to another during 2. Download Logs – here the user can download the logs to be reviewed/stored offline. Note: The file downloaded will display the logs based on how the screen has been filtered (if filters are applied). 3. Audit History display – This displays the log in table form including each change/update by: • Date & Time • Event Group • Event From • Event To • User Name • Comments – This will display any comment added at the time of the change. • Type- Transaction/Return • ID Comply: Returns Processing 8. Reviewer The Reviewer (again if they have configured their notifications), will receive the notification email that they have a return to action. And the return will be displayed in the Assigned to Me section of their returns screen in Comply. The job of the reviewer is to open and review the data in each of the following tabs to ensure the preparer has not missed anything and to ensure it is in good order before sending for Approval: Comply: Returns Processing Data Validation The reviewer will check for any errors where required.

Transactions The Reviewer will check the transaction data for any missing or errors in the data. Next Page Comply: Returns Processing Return Validation Again here, the Reviewer is just checking the work completed by the Preparer, ensuring the validation of the data against the rules is complete and in good order. Return Review approval. The Reviewer here can review the final values and view the return files before sending for Please note, if there are any issues found at this stage the user can Reject the return, in which case it reverts back to a Status of To Prepare and is returned to the Preparer for review. Comply: Returns Processing 8.1. Send for Approval If all is in good order, then the Reviewer simply clicks the Send for Approval button. This changes the status to To Approve. Based on the schedule due date for the Approval step, a notification email is sent to the Approver that there is a return for them to action. Please note: The user can leave a comment (If there is key information for the Approver to know). That completes the Reviewer process. Comply: Returns Processing 9. Approver Approving the return. The Approver essentially repeats the same data checks as the Reviewer before rejecting or Once reviewed, the user clicks Approve. This changes the status automatically to To Submit. That completes the Approver process and triggers the notification mail to be sent to the Submitter. Comply: Returns Processing 10. Submitter The Submitter will either log in directly to Comply or via a notification email advising that the return has been approved in is ready to be submitted. Here the Submitter has the option to review the return details again or simply Submit the return. To do this, the user simply: 1. Open the Return. 2. Click the Return Review tab. 3. Click the Submit button. (if they are happy with the data). 4. This changes the status of the return to “Submitting”. Once this changes to Submitted, this automatically triggers an immediate Email Alert to the Approver and/or Treasurer advising the return has been successfully submitted and they should make payment.

Introduction 1.1. What is SAF-T? SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) is a data standard that was implemented by some EU Jurisdictions in order to improve the efficiency and accuracy of tax compliance. In short, it’s a way for businesses to provide standardized data to tax authorities in order to facilitate audits and reduce the risk of errors. The idea behind SAF-T is simple enough: by making it easier for tax authorities to access accurate information, businesses can avoid being hit with hefty fines for errors or inaccuracies in their tax filings. 1.2. Who does this apply to? At present SAF-T is not mandatory in most Jurisdictions. In fact, only Poland, Portugal, Norway and Romania have made it mandatory to date. Requirements differ by Jurisdiction and as such, some countries may be required to report the following relevant data: • Sales • Purchases data • Both (Sales and Purchases) i.e. Poland are required to report both Sales and Purchase 1.3. What does this mean? When filing a return, for SAF-T, the relevant additional boxes will be generated for the Return. Example: For Poland, the requirement is to generate both List Sales and List Purchases, both boxes will be generated and displayed in the Return Review tab (Numerical Boxes) in Comply. Please note: Where a Jurisdiction requires only List Sales or List Purchases, only one box will be generated and displayed in Comply. 2. text: 12th Nov 2022 Keith O’Sullivan Published 1.1. Purpose of this document The scheduler allows the user to configure the number of days it will take to complete each stage in the return process. It then calculates the completion dates for each step. This ensures that the return is submitted on-time by the submission deadline. There are 5 stages which must be set, these are: • Data Due • To Prepare • To Review • To Approve • To Submit Note: The number of days between each stage is set by default but the user may decide to amend this timeframe. 1.2. Configuring the Scheduler To set up the scheduler the user should follow these steps: 1. Go to the Navigation menu. 2. Click the Settings sub menu. 3. Click Scheduler. 4. Select the Entity drop-down menu to set the scheduler for. Note: You will need to set a schedule for each entity. 5. Click the arrow on the selected jurisdiction to open the scheduler. This opens the VAT Return displaying 2 schedule options: • VAT Return Scheduler • Payment Scheduler – This relates to TBI Pay and will be covered in a later relevant guide. For the VAT Return Scheduler, the most important date to consider is the Submission Date. This is the date by which the VAT Return must be submitted, anything outside of this, the return will be considered late and may incur penalties. So when considering the scheduler and each of the stages of the return the user should start with the Submission Date and work backwards. 6. Click the drop-down option on each of stages of the return and select the number of days the user needs to complete the process. Example: Working backwards from the Submission Date of e.g. 25th Nov 2021: It will take no time for the return to be submitted from the return is submitted. It will take 3 days to submit from when it is approved. It will take 3 days to approve from when it is reviewed. It will take 1 day to review from when it is prepared. It will take 3 days to prepare from when the data is received. 7. Reminder: Complete this process for each Entity. - - - - - Note 1: The user can choose to filter out Weekends in the scheduler. E.g. If 2 days are required to complete a stage, the user can set the scheduler to ignore weekends, and will include working days only as part of this 2-day timeframe. Note 2: The user can also choose to filter out Public Holidays in the scheduler. E.g. If 2 days or more are required to complete any stage, the user can set the scheduler to ignore public holidays and will include the working days only as part of the timeline. Regarding the public holidays, this is based on the country where the user is based for at stage. 1.2.1. Viewing the schedule To view the future returns schedule: 1. Click View Scheduler. The scheduler is populated with future returns and has calculated the dates required for each stage of each return. 1.2.2. Manually Change Specific Future Dates The user can choose to manually amend a specific date, for a specific stage, for a specific return. E.g. Change the To Approve date, on the Jan 2022 return. To do this: 1. Open the Scheduler. 2. Click View Scheduler. 3.

E.g. Change the To Approve date, on the Jan 2022 return. To do this: 1. Open the Scheduler. 2. Click View Scheduler. 3. Click on the date box of the To Approve stage of the required return. 4. Type in the new date required. Once the user amends a date(s) for any return, those date fields are highlighted in green. Note: This change will trigger a recalculation of the dates in the previous stages for that return. Purpose of this document The purpose of this document is to provide instruction on the creation, configuration and management of Validation Rules. 3. Introduction 3.1. What are the Validation Rules? Comply comes preconfigured with Rules which help automate the validation of returns data. These include: • Standard Rules: • Custom Rules rules. level. o There are 290 + built in rules. o These include VAT, VIES and Intrastat rules. o These are split between Mandatory and Configurable rules. o Depending on the contract type, clients can avail of a number of customisable o Custom rules can be configured by Admin Users. o These can be configured/enabled at Return Type, Jurisdiction and/or Entity Please note: Only Admin users of Comply can view/configure rules Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 3.2. Errors and Warnings Validation rules are designed to provide validation and once triggered may display an Error or a Description processed. An error occurs where there is a problem with mandatory values or data which must be rectified before the VAT Return can continue to be i.e. This could be an incorrect/missing VAT Rate for the jurisdiction, which stops the required calculations across numerical boxes. Warning If triggered, a warning is used to bring attention to data which is outside the validation criteria but which is not mandatory and does not stop the return being processed or filed. i.e. This could be a value which is outside a configured threshold or average. The variance from previous periods could be high or low and the warning is in place to review for potential flags. Warning. Type Error Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 4. Standard Rules As outlined above, Standard Rules include a suite of preconfigured validation rules. These rules are run against the uploaded data file to ensure all the data for the return is in good order. Navigation: Settings > Validation Rules > Standard Rules Comply: Configuring Validation Rules The Standard Rules screen is comprised of a table of rules displayed across 4 columns. The majority of these rules are mandatory and are by default locked for editing. 1. Rule ID – This column lists designated ID’s related to VAT rules. 2. Validation – This column provides a description of the rule. 3. Error Type – There are 2 Error Types: Error or Warning. 4. Active – Most Standard Rules are mandatory and will be configured during the Onboarding Process. Some rules will have an option to be Enabled or Disabled. However some rules can be further configured/managed. 5. If the Gear icon is visible, Validation Rules may be edited by Admin user. 4.1. Configurable Rules Where a rule is configurable, the user is presented with multiple options: • Change the Error Type from a Warning to and Error or vice versa. • Enable/Disable the Rule. • Configure the rule to apply to certain attributes only i.e. Return Types/Jurisdictions/Entities. Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 4.1.1. Change the Error Type To change the error type, select either Error or Warning from the drop-down menu. 4.1.2. Enable/Disable the Rule Turn the Toggle switch on/off as required. 4.1.3. Set rule behaviour PL 1 1. Click the Cog.

Select UK from the Tax Jurisdiction drop-down menu and click Apply (again multiple 4. Select Entity PL1 from the Entity drop-down menu and click Apply (again multiple can be selected). options can be selected if required) . options can be selected if required) . Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 5. Select Save. The rule setting is applied. The following message is displayed to confirm that the relevant mapping has been updated to reflect the new rule settings. Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 6. Select Add to create additional settings if required. These can also be deleted at any time by clicking the Bin Icon beside the rule setting. Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 5. Custom Rules Depending on the clients contract, different plans allow varying allocations of Custom Rules up to a maximum of 20. This allows the client to create specific rules which apply to their own requirements. 5.1. Creating a Custom Rule Navigation: Settings > Validation Rules > Custom Rules 5.1.1. How to Create a Custom Validation Rule Click ‘Add A New Rule’ or ‘Create a Rule’. Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 1. Enter a Name for the new Rule. All rules consist of an “If” statement and a “Then” statement. • If Statements contain the “what” component of the rule, this tells the system to look out for certain criteria or data. • Then Statements contain the behaviour component, this tells the system what to do when the data in the If Statement has been triggered. 2. Adding Conditions a. Select from which template you wish to add the rule (TBI or Client Template Field) b. Select the field to be validated. c. Select the validation terms (Blank/Less than/Equal to etc). Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 3. (Optional) Select And/Or if you wish to add additional If Conditions to be validated. Selecting an option here requires a new If Statement to be configured. 4. Add the Then Statement: This is the behaviour you wish the system to perform when ALL the IF conditions are met. a. Display Error b. Display Warning 5. Add Text. This is a free form text field. Add a brief description of the Error or Warning. This will be displayed when an error or warning is triggered. 6. Add Error Solution. This is a free form field. Add a suggested solution/guidance for the error or warning. This will be displayed for the user once an error or warning is triggered. Comply: Configuring Validation Rules 7. Click Apply. A success message is displayed confirming the rule has been added. The Rule is now added to the Custom Rules screen. EC Sales List and EC Purchase List
THIS IS A EUROPEAN UNION MEMBER STATE REQUIREMENT ONLY
VIES stands for VAT Information Exchange System and is an electronic means of transmitting information relating to VAT registration of companies registered in the European Union.
This obligation to file an The EC Sales List (ESL) sometimes called a Recapulative Statement is a reporting obligation for VAT Registered entities operating within the EU.
The EC Sales List or ESL return is an informative reporting obligation that must be submitted when a transfer goods or supply of services takes place from one EU country to another EU country, i.e., when you perform intra-Community Supplies of goods and services. The purpose of the reporting is to ensure that the appropriate amount of VAT is being paid and declared by all relevant parties in these transactions.
What is the difference between Intrastat and EC Sales List Filing
Intrastat is a different reporting obligation which provides the EU authorities and governments further and more detailed information on the movements of goods within the European Union than the EC sales list, for statistical purposes.
Intrastat is a statistical return and EC Sales list is a tax return. Intrastat is sent to customs and statistical authorities whereas EC Sales is submitted in the portal of your usual tax returns. They both cover intra-Community transactions, but the scope of the information included is different in Intrastat and EC Sale Listings.
France, Poland, Romania, Spain also require an EC Purchase List (EPL) to be filed in addition to the EC Sales List. No such obligation exists for the other countries.
Revisions for VIES are supported in Comply. There are changes required for enhanced support for Hungary, Estonia, Slovakia, Croatia these are part of a future release.

Purpose of this section The purpose of this document is to provide guidance and instruction on how Comply users submit Returns for Finland using an API with the Finish Tax Authority. It will cover the steps required for Configuring Comply and for both Successful and Failed Submission flows. An API integration is now available in Comply which allows the submission of returns to the 1.2. Overview Finnish Tax Authority. 1.2.1. Return Types • VAT Returns • EC Sales The following Return Types only can be submitted via API. Comply : API Submission (Finland) 2. External Configuration (Acquiring Certificate) Comply provides the user with the ability within Comply to file Submissions via an API (Digital Filing). In order for this to be used, a Certificate (Authentication) needs to be issued which allows a Foreign Representative to complete the filing. There are 3 key components to this configuration: The client must Assign/Authorise the TBI Representative to Acquire the Certificate. The TBI Rep. completes the application for using the Interface. Retrieval of the Certificate Please note: All of these are completed outside of Comply. 2.1. Assign/Authorise the TBI Representative to Acquire the Certificate The client must Register/Login to https://vero.fi/en/incomes-register/ Follow the Instructions to Submit an Application for Production Certificate. The client must then go to https://www.vero.fi/en/incomes-register/companies-and- organisations/Use-our-services-electronically/grant-authorisation/foreign-companies/ Follow the Instructions to authorise the TBI Representative to act on behalf of the client. TBI Representative Details: Name: First Name, Surname Finnish Foreigners User Identifier (UID): 545310351F Mandate Theme: Processing log, interface and report data related to income data. • • • 1. 2. 3. 4. • • • Comply : API Submission (Finland) 2.2. TBI Representative Applies for the Certificate Login to: https://tunnistautuminen.suomi.fi/sivut/500/?t=2405281128f37f&m=discoveryRender Select the Company applying for the Certificate. On the Companies page, select Settings > Technical Interface. Check that the purpose of use of the interface indicated at Valid rights is “Earnings payment data, organisation reports the wages it has paid and Earnings payment data, organisation reports wages on behalf of another party”, and that the channel selection is “Earnings payment data – Web Service”. Other rights may also be selected. 5. If the purpose of use is not reporting earnings payment data and the channel selection is not Web Service, then you must submit a replacement application. Select Make a replacement application. 6. In the replacement application, tick the following options in addition to any other options already selected: at purpose of use of the interface, tick “Earnings payment data, organisation reports the wages it has paid and Earnings payment data, organisation reports wages on behalf of another party”, and at channel, tick “Earnings payment data – Web Service”.

The replacement application replaces all previous selections, so make sure the application contains all the purposes of use and all the channels that the company needs. 7. When your right to access the interface has been verified, make the certificate application: Certificates > Apply for a new certificate. Select “Earnings payment data – Web Service” as the type of production certificate. Production certificate users must accept and follow the terms and conditions of use for the Tax Administration’s and the Incomes Register’s interface services (available in pdf format in Finnish and Swedish, link to Finnish) 10. You must specify a technical contact person in the certificate application. The technical contact person retrieves the certificate from the certificate service interface. 1. 2. 3. 4. 8. 9. A secure email is sent to the Technical Contact Person with instruction for retrieving the The production certificate is retrieved from the production address of the certificate service's Web Service interface: https://pkiws.vero.fi/2017/10/CertificateServices (TCP port 443) 1. They will receive a text message on their mobile phone containing a PIN for opening the secure e-mail message. The PIN will be sent after the contact person has clicked the “Open message” link on the secure e-mail message they received when they applied for the certificate. The certificate must be retrieved from the certificate service interface within 14 days after you submitted the application. 2. After successful retrieval, the technical contact person specified in the application imports the certificate into the software. If the user organisation does not have a valid certificate, Vero API will not transmit the records the organisation requests. Please Note: Vero API responds to calls made with production certificates only after the certificate has been retrieved and installed in the organisation’s environment. Certificates for Vero API are retrieved from the Incomes Register's certificate service. In general, production certificates generated in the certificate service during office hours (8.00 am to 4.15 pm) will work in Vero API calls at the latest on the following day. Comply : API Submission (Finland) 3. Submitting Submit button is available. The API submission process begins when the status on a return is at “To Submit” and the Once the user clicks Submit, the Return Submitted Pop-Up is displayed. This outlines that the Return has been submitted to the Tax Authority for processing. Please Note: This is an interim status to reflect that the return is being processed by the Tax Authority. Audit History A log is added to the Audit History. The return file has been submitted and now goes through a Tax Authority Data Validation process. Depending on the response from the Tax Authority, the Return will be either Successful or Failed, and Comply will be updated with the relevant response and relevant Status change. Comply : API Submission (Finland) 3.1. Successful Submission Flow When the response is received from the Tax Authority, and the response is processed the following are triggered simultaneously. Status Change The status of the return changes to Submitted. Submission Results The Submission Confirmation is added to the Submission Results tab on the Return Review screen. text: 18th Oct 2023 Keith O’Sullivan Published Comply : API Submission (Germany) 1. Introduction 1.1. Purpose of this section The purpose of this document is to provide guidance and instruction on how Comply users submit Returns for Germany using an API. It will cover the steps required for Configuring Comply and for both Successful and Failed Submission flows. 1.2. Overview To exchange data with the German Tax authority (via Eric), you need one or more certificates which are password protected and as such it is important to have the required PIN/Password. For the API submission, the correct combination of PFX Certificate & PIN/Password must be added in the backend of Comply. This step is currently configured by opening a JIRA ticket with the support desk to have this added. 1.2.1. Return Types All Return Types can be submitted via API. • VAT Returns • VIES • Annual Returns • VAT Advanced Payments Comply : API Submission (Germany) 2. Tax Office Authorisation (External Steps) In order to submit your filings digitally (Via API), the client must complete the following: 1. Register on Mein Elster https://www.elster.de/eportal/login/softpse 2. Request a PFX Certificate and PIN. This certificate is the secure authorisation which allows comply to communicate digitally with the German Tax Authority on the clients behalf when submitting returns. 3. Send the PFX Certificate and PIN to TBI via Encrypted Email. Comply : API Submission (Germany) 3. Configuration (In Comply) If a Tax Consultant is filing on behalf of a client, then no action is required here. If a client is filing on their own behalf, or if a Foreign Tax Consultant is filing on their behalf, then some configuration steps are required. 3.1. Select Submitter Information The XML files generated for each Submitter Type vary in type and consist of different data. Selecting the Submitter Type here ensures the correct XML template which will be generated. 1. Go to Settings. 2. Open the Entity sub-menu. This opens the Entity Details page. 1. In the Entity section, select the relevant Entity. 2. Click the Jurisdiction in the Jurisdiction Country Details section. 3. Click Visit This Page. Comply : API Submission (Germany) Here in the Jurisdiction Details page, you can set the Filer Type. The options here are: Filer Type Entrepreneur Description A Tax Consultant filing for you. Filing on your own behalf You are filing on your own behalf. Foreign Entrepreneur A Foreign Tax Consultant is filing on your behalf. Please note: By default, this section is set to Entrepreneur. Comply : API Submission (Germany) 3.2. Changing the Default Submitter Type If you change the submitter type, you must click Save at the bottom on the screen, at which point you will receive the following notification pop-ups. 3.2.1. File as an Entrepreneur on your own behalf: 3.2.2. Foreign Entrepreneur: Please note: If you select the Foreign Entrepreneur option, then you are required to complete the Fiscal Representative Details section on screen. Comply : API Submission (Germany) Comply : API Submission (Germany) 3.3. Add PFX Certificate and PIN What if no PFX Certificate/PIN has been added to your Entity?

Comply : API Submission (Germany) Comply : API Submission (Germany) 3.3. Add PFX Certificate and PIN What if no PFX Certificate/PIN has been added to your Entity? In the case where neither a PFX Certificate and/or PIN have been added to your entity, then the following will be displayed on the return. Please note: This Notification appears on all Statuses and for all user roles (Preparer/Reviewer/Approver). In this scenario, the user has two options: • Option 1: Open a JIRA Request • Option 2: Submit It Manually Comply : API Submission (Germany) 3.3.1. Open a JIRA Ticket 1. Open a JIRA ticket requesting an email link which can be shared with the client by onboarding to securely send their PFX Certificate and PIN. Below is a sample ticket. 2. The onboarding team will forward the link to the client. 3. The client should use the link to send their PFX Certificate and PIN to TBI which in turn is added to relevant client account. 4. Once completed, the user can log back into Comply and Resubmit the return. Comply : API Submission (Germany) 3.3.2. Submit it Manually If it is time sensitive, the user can elect to Process the Return and Submit it Manually. 1. Go to Return Review. 2. Download the XML file. 3. Log Into the Tax Authority Portal. 4. Upload the File. Comply : API Submission (Germany) 4. Submitting Once the return status in Comply is as “To Submit”: 1. Click Submit. The return data is exchanged with ERiC via the API and goes through 2 Validation Steps: • Authentication Process • Data Validation Please note: These are both Tax Authority processes. Comply : API Submission (Germany) 4.1. Tax Authority Authentication The Authentication process of your PFX Certificate and Password combination is completed by the German Tax Authorities upon clicking the Submit button in Comply. 4.1.1. Authorisation Failed If an Invalid Certificate or PIN/Password were uploaded. This triggers the following five things which happen simultaneously: • Error Pop-up • Submission Status The Submission Status is changed to Submission Failed. Comply : API Submission (Germany) • Submission Results The Submission Results tab is updated. In this example, the Tax Authority Data Validation tab displays an error icon, and the error is displayed below. Any errors found during validation of the submission trigger an automatic email to the • Email Notification Preparer/Reviewer/Submitter. Comply : API Submission (Germany) • Audit History The Audit History is automatically updated with a Submission failed log. 4.1.2. Solutions In this example, the user has two options: • Update Certificate/Password 1. Open a JIRA ticket requesting the Relevant PFX Certificate and Password be added. 3. The client will be provided a link to an encrypted email to provide TBI with the PFX 2. The following are required on the ticket: • CRM ID of Client • Client name Certificate and PIN/Password. 4. These details are then added to the Client account. When ticket is completed then the return can be re-submitted.

Comply : API Submission (Germany) This option allows the user to skip the API transmission and submit the return manually. • Submit Manually 1. Click Submit Manually. 2. Go to Return Review. 3. Download the XML file. 4. Log Into the Tax Authority Portal. 5. Upload the File. 6. Click Complete. Comply : API Submission (Germany) 4.2. Return to “To Prepare” If required, The Return to “To Prepare” button is displayed on the following Statuses: • To Submit • Submission Failed Example: Submission Failed This will allow the user to bring the status back to “To Prepare” and make any relevant changes. text: 28th June Keith O’Sullivan Release Update Purpose of this document The purpose of this document is to provide guidance, context, and instruction for users to successfully onboard and configure a new client onto the Comply platform. The following Steps are required to successfully complete this process: Note: This process can only be completed by users who have been assigned Administrator access. 1. Login To login to the platform, the user is sent an email from Taxback International (TBI) including a link and password for the Vault. https://login.taxbackinternational.com/login 1.1. Login Steps 1. Open the link provided in the email. 2. Enter the username and password. 3. Click Continue. 4. Select VAT Comply Platform The default landing page after logging in is the Global Dashboard. This can also be found at any point, by navigating to the Analytics menu. 2. User Configuration 2.1. Security Menu The Security menu provides the user with data relating to user profiles, system credentials and permissions. The sub menus displayed here will depend on the permissions and profile of the user, i.e. • Standard User • Administrator 2.1.1. Standard User The standard user will see only the User Details sub menu. This is essentially a read only screen, displaying the system and role credentials for the user, which was predefined at the initial account creation. This will include: User Details • Personal Details • Report Role – these are the specific VAT return roles the user has been assigned to for any entities they are responsible for. • Settings: o Access Type – Full or Partial Access. o Account Status o Account created date o Last Log on o Escalation Trigger – The number of days after which an overdue task will be escalated to the assigned Escalation user (TBI or Client user – if configured). o Notification Preferences – The frequency the user receives system reminders for tasks assigned to them. 2.1.2. Standard User Notifications This preconfigured process allows the user to receive system reminders via email for tasks that are assigned to them. I.e. if the user is assigned as Data Provider, Preparer, Reviewer or Approver etc for certain returns. If they are assigned tasks based on any of the roles outlined in the return process, then this allows the user to set the frequency of when they receive such reminders. Note: The reminders will be sent to the email address assigned in the user profile. Below as a sample of an email reminder: If the user is responsible for multiple roles and multiple returns, they may be combined and grouped appropriately. The user is advised to login to Comply and take the necessary action(s). 2.1.3. Administrator The Administrator has additional permissions, and as such the profile displays the following 3 sub menus: • User Details • User Management • User Roles User Details This displays the system and role credentials for the user, which was predefined at the initial • Report Role – these are the specific VAT return roles the user has been assigned to for account creation. This will include: • Personal Details any entities they are responsible for. • Settings: o Access Type o Account Status o Account created date o Last Log on o Notification Preferences – The frequency the user receives system reminders o Escalation Trigger – The number of days after which an overdue task will be for tasks assigned to them. escalated to the user. User Management As an administrator, the user can view, manage and edit all existing users.

User Management As an administrator, the user can view, manage and edit all existing users. 1. The Administrator can click the edit button on any existing user to make changes to that profile (Including Activating and Deactivating user profiles). This brings them to an editable version of the User Details screen for the selected user. 2. The Administrator can bulk import new members. The user can upload or drag and drop an existing prepopulated file from another location. 3. The Administrator can Manually add a new user. 4. Filter the list of existing users to display only those unique to a specific role(s). User Roles Here the administrator can assign/edit roles to each task in the VAT Return process. These tasks may assigned to: • Client • System • Taxback International (TBI) Staff Note 1: Each Entity could potentially consist of multiple jurisdictions. If so, they will appear here, and roles/users should be assigned to tasks for each jurisdiction as required. Note 2: If the same roles/users are to be assigned to the same tasks for each jurisdiction, the user can select the roles from the drop-down options beside “Apply to All”. Note 3: Different users can also be assigned to different/multiple deliverables i.e. VAT Return/Intrastat/VIES per 1 VAT Number. To assign a role/user to a task, the user can select the relevant user from the drop-down menu under a specific task. Note: This is currently sorted alphabetically. 3. Initial Company Configuration The user must now configure the Company on the Comply platform. This process includes several steps which the system leads the user through. To complete this process: 1. Go to the Navigation menu. 2. Click the Settings sub menu. 3. Click Onboarding. each step. 4. Complete the steps numbered above in the screenshot. See below for more details on 3.1. Set up your Company Details The user is required to upload the relevant company data to Comply. To do this: 1. Download the Template. 2. Complete the spreadsheet. Note: All columns highlighted in yellow are Mandatory fields. Tip: Users should always check if an entity already exists before creating a new one. And in the case where a user is creating a new jurisdiction for an existing Company, they should review and ensure consistency with existing data. 3. Save the completed file. 4. Once complete, the user can: a. Drag and Drop the saved file back into Comply. b. Browse for and upload the file to Comply. 5. Click Submit. 3.2. Set up your List of Users The user is now required to upload the relevant company users to Comply. To do this: 1. Download the Template. 2. Open the downloaded .xlsx file. 3. Complete the spreadsheet. Note: All columns highlighted in yellow are Mandatory fields. 4. Once saved, the user can: a. Drag and Drop the saved file to Comply. b. Browse for and upload the saved file to Comply. 5. Click Submit. Note: In the case where users already exist, the Administrator can upload a blank user set up template. This essentially skips this process where required. 3.3. Set up User Roles The user is now required to assign roles to each task in the VAT Return process. A user must be selected for each mandatory role in Comply per jurisdiction.

This essentially skips this process where required. 3.3. Set up User Roles The user is now required to assign roles to each task in the VAT Return process. A user must be selected for each mandatory role in Comply per jurisdiction. The Mandatory roles are: • Data Provider – person responsible for providing the data for the return. • Preparer – person responsible for preparing the return. • Reviewer – person responsible for reviewing the return. • Approver – person responsible for approving the return. • Submitter – person responsible for submitting the return. . These roles may be assigned to any of the following groups: • Client Staff • System Bots • Taxback International (TBI) Staff Note 1: A Company could potentially consist of multiple jurisdictions. If so, they will appear here, and roles/users should be assigned to tasks for each jurisdiction as required. Note 2: If the same roles/users are to be assigned to the same tasks for each jurisdiction, the user can select the roles from the drop-down options beside “Apply to All”. To assign a role/user to a task: 1. Select the relevant user from the drop-down menu under a specific task. 2. Complete for all relevant roles. 3. Click Submit. Note 1 - It may be the case that the Preparer and Submitter is the same person, but there are rules built in to prevent the Preparer and Reviewer from being the same person. Note 2 – The Reviewer and Approver roles can be assigned to the system user which will automatically approve the return for that stage in the process. This can be assigned in situations where the data provided does not require calculations or is ready for submission. Note 3 – Additional non-mandatory roles are also available for completion • Payment Approver – Applies to TBI Pay service. • Treasurer – Applies to TBI Pay service. • Escalation TBI – more than one approved user can be appointed here as a point of • Escalation Client – more than one approved user can be appointed here as a point of escalation. escalation. 4. Complete the same process for each Jurisdiction. 4. Configure the Scheduler 4.1. Overview The scheduler allows the user to configure the number of days it will take to complete each stage in the return process. It then calculates the completion dates for each step. This ensures that the return is submitted on-time by the submission deadline. There are 5 stages which must be set, these are: • Data Due • To Prepare • To Review • To Approve • To Submit Note: The number of days between each stage is set by default but the user may decide to amend this timeframe. 4.2. Setting the Scheduler To set up the scheduler the user should follow these steps: 1. Go to the Navigation menu. 2. Click the Settings sub menu. 3. Click Scheduler. 4. Select the Entity drop-down menu to set the scheduler for. Note: You will need to set a schedule for each entity. 5. Click the arrow on the selected jurisdiction to open the scheduler. This opens the VAT Return displaying 2 schedule options: • VAT Return Scheduler • Payment Scheduler – This relates to TBI Pay and will be covered in a later relevant guide. For the VAT Return Scheduler, the most important date to consider is the Submission Date.

For the VAT Return Scheduler, the most important date to consider is the Submission Date. This is the date by which the VAT Return must be submitted, anything outside of this, the return will be considered late and may incur penalties. So when considering the scheduler and each of the stages of the return the user should start with the Submission Date and work backwards. 6. Click the drop-down option on each of stages of the return and select the number of days the user needs to complete the process. Example: Working backwards from the Submission Date of e.g. 25th Nov 2021: - Once submitted, the status updates immediately. - - - - It will take 3 days to submit from when it is approved. It will take 3 days to approve from when it is reviewed. It will take 1 day to review from when it is prepared. It will take 3 days to prepare from when the data is received. 7. Reminder: Complete this process for each Entity. Note 1: The user can choose to filter out Weekends in the scheduler. E.g. If 2 days are required to complete a stage, the user can set the scheduler to ignore weekends, and will include working days only as part of this 2-day timeframe. Note 2: The user can also choose to filter out Public Holidays in the scheduler. E.g. If 2 days or more are required to complete any stage, the user can set the scheduler to ignore public holidays and will include the working days only as part of the timeline. Regarding the public holidays, this is based on the country where the user is based for at stage. 4.2.1. Viewing the schedule To view the future returns schedule: 1. Click View Scheduler. The scheduler is populated with future returns and has calculated the dates required for each stage of each return. 4.2.2. Manually Change Specific Future Dates The user can choose to manually amend a specific date, for a specific stage, for a specific return. E.g. Change the To Approve date, on the Jan 2022 return. To do this: 1. Open the Scheduler. 2. Click View Scheduler. 3. Click on the date box of the To Approve stage of the required return. 4. Type in the new date required. Once the user amends a date(s) for any return, those date fields are highlighted in green. Note: This change will trigger a recalculation of the dates in the previous stages for that return. 5. Configure the Data Transformation Template 5.1. Why is a Data Transformation Template Required? Clients onboarding to Comply, in most cases use Excel files downloaded from their own ERP systems to file returns. Each of these files contain transactional data with vast numbers of Columns. The naming convention and meanings of these columns of data may differ to what TBI looks for. So Comply needs to “understand” the clients data, and process it accurately. 5.2. What is a Data Transformation Template? A Data Transformation Template allows the user to upload a sample file from their system, and map the relevant fields to the relevant TBI fields and create rules which define the meaning of values in certain fields. Once configured, every time their data is imported to TBI via an API, Comply uses the template to auto transform their data without the need for manual intervention.

Once configured, every time their data is imported to TBI via an API, Comply uses the template to auto transform their data without the need for manual intervention. To do this, the user must complete the following processes: • Create a Data Template. • Map the data to the TBI fields. • Assign a Template to a Return. To complete this configuration Comply has a specific Templates are on the Menu. There are 3 sub menus: • Create Template • Existing Template • Assign Template Create a Template The user must define how the Comply platform should recognize the fields of information in the client’s data file which are required to upload to a return. 5.2.1. Create the new template: 1. Extract a sample report of the data from the client’s ERP system (this should be the report normally used by the client when preparing VAT returns). 2. In Comply, click on Templates on the Menu. 3. Click the Create Template sub-menu. 4. Click the Name the Template field and type a name for the template. 5. Select a Return Type from the Return Types drop-down menu. Please note: Depending on the selection made here, the user will be required to complete different next steps. VAT Related Returns: By selecting this option, you are then asked to select the relevant Tax Jurisdiction(s). Intrastat Arrivals/Dispatches: Return SubTypes drop-down menu. Buy selecting Intrastat Arrivals/Dispatches, the user must then make a selection from the This will also require the user to select the relevant Jurisdiction(s). 6. Chose a file or simply drag and drop a file from wherever the file is located locally. Once the new template has been created, the user must map the data uploaded to the mandatory fields/columns required by TBI. Comply will lead you through the relevant screens to • Identify additional File Name Information. • Set Data Transformation Rules/Tax Treatments/Other Transformation Rules/Date & 7. Click Save. complete the following: • Map the fields. • Map the Codes. Number Formats. 5.2.2. Map the Data to the TBI fields pre-defined TBI fields on the Right. Comply displays the list of the column headers uploaded from the client file on the left and the There are a number of screens to complete. On each one, match up the required column headers by dragging and dropping them into the TBI fields. This instructs Comply which columns hold the required data. 1. This displays the progress of the template creation process. 2. This is a list view of the users imported fields. 3. You can use the Search feature to locate specific fields when mapping them to TBI fields. This is useful when you have imported a large number of fields. 4. This is a list of the required TBI fields. You will need to match your imported fields to these if required. 5. Where mandatory fields are missing, you will be prompted here. Clicking this link will open a list of Mandatory fields you will need to map. Note: The user should map as many TBI fields as possible, however Mandatory fields are marked with a red Asterix. 1. Tax Data This first screen requires the user to match Tax specific data fields.

Note: The user should map as many TBI fields as possible, however Mandatory fields are marked with a red Asterix. 1. Tax Data This first screen requires the user to match Tax specific data fields. Mandatory Fields: • Tax Jurisdiction ISO Code • Tax Period • Tax Year • Transaction Type • Transaction Category • Goods Services Category Note 1: Not all the TBI fields may get mapped at this point but the client can map file name information or create data transformation rules in subsequent screens to complete the mapping – discussed below in Create Data Transformation Rules. 2. Supplier/Customer Data Here the user should map specific Sales and/or Purchases data. Although there are no mandatory fields here, it is recommended that the user map there Supplier or Customer related data. 3. Invoice Data Map the clients Invoice data, i.e. Supplier or Customer Invoice details. Mandatory actions here require the user to map the following: • Supplier Invoice Date & Customer Invoice Date Or • Sales/Purchase Invoice Date 4. VAT Rate/VAT-ID Data The user should map their own date for VAT Rate and VAT ID/VAT Reference data. Mandatory actions here require the user to map the following: • Purchases VAT Rate & Sales VAT Rate Or • VAT Rate 5. Country Codes From Country data. These are not mandatory, but if necessary, the user can map country codes for Ship to and Ship 6. Currency Codes and FX The user should map currency codes for both Sales and Purchase transactions. Mandatory actions here require the user to map the following: • Supplier Transaction Currency Name & Customer Transaction Currency Or • Sales/Purchase Transaction Currency 7. Monetary Values The user is required to map the relevant fields for Sales and/or Purchase Net values. Mandatory actions here require the user to map the following: • Purchase Net Amount & Sales Net Amount or Sales/Purchase Net Amount • Purchase VAT Amount & Sales VAT Amount or Sales/Purchase VAT Amount Or 8. Monetary Values Tax Jurisdiction Currency If relevant, the user should map any relevant fields which identify values in the currency of a specific tax jurisdiction. These are not mandatory, but are recommended where these values are required in specific currencies. 9. Other Fields here. The user/client may have custom fields/values which they wish to import. If so they can do so 10. Intrastat / VIES platform. Where Intrastat/VIES reporting is relevant, the user can map relevant data fields to the Comply 5.2.3. 1 to Many Mapping Comply also allows the user, to map fields in the Client data to a TBI field more than once (where the TBI field is a required field in more than one mapping screen). After dragging and dropping a client field, the header remains in the “All Columns From Your Excel” section to be used again if necessary. It also displays a numerical icon identifying how many times the header has been mapped. 5.2.4. Map the Tax Transaction Codes The user must now define/configure the Tax Transaction Codes. Please Note: If the user accesses this screen via “Existing Template”, any current values and mappings will be displayed here and can be edited accordingly (depending on the users profile). text:
Intrastat Reporting
Intrastat is the system for collecting information and producing statistics on the trade in goods between countries of the European Union. The Intrastat reporting is a monthly obligation for those companies moving goods across the EU which surpass those countries reporting thresholds.
There is only one frequency allowed which is monthly.
There is no electronic mechanism provided by any Country to file Intrastat reports. They must be loaded via the portals provided by the tax authority.
United Kingdom is not required to file Intrastat post brexit. Northern Ireland which is under the UK is required to file Intrastat.

2. Templates – Txt File Delimiters
When preparing a template in Comply and the Txt file upload includes delimiters in the headers,
Comply identifies these and automatically extracts the correct values to create the template
successfully.
What are delimiters?
A delimiter is a sequence of one or more characters for specifying the boundary between
separate, independent regions in plain text, mathematical expressions, or other data streams. An
example of a delimiter is the comma character, which acts as a field delimiter in a sequence of
comma-separated values.

following Pop-up message.
3.2. Move to Different Return
When preparing a return and the user has clicked the Move to a Different Return option, then
only the relevant return type options will be displayed to choose from.
For example, if preparing a VAT Return, then the user can only move a transaction to another
VAT Return. The same applies for VIES/Control Lists/Annual Client Listings/Annual Returns.
Example: Move from a VAT Return. Only VAT Returns are displayed to which it can be moved to.

1. VAT Groups
The following are updates to Comply as they relate to VAT Groups.
1.1. Members Leaving (VCCMVP-4062)
Description:
As a Comply Admin user and member of a VAT Group, if you leave a VAT Group all future
unsubmitted VAT Group Returns will become returns of a standalone entity. This will allow
easier filing for separate and not grouped returns.
1.2. Deregistration – Entity/Member of VAT Group (VCCMVP-5115)
Description:
As an Admin Staff/Client User, when a user deregisters an entity from a VAT Group then the
VAT Group Details>Part of a VAT Group? automatically updates from Yes to No and the set Is
VAT Group Representative updates to blank.
This means that system updates will be in line with the Deregistration of that Entity.
1.3. Deletion of Data Files – VAT Group (VCCMVP-5350)
Description:
As a Comply user, when a Data File for an Individual or VAT Calculation Return is deleted from a
Consolidated Return the system removes these transactions. This ensures that the wrong
transactions are not submitted.
Comply: Release Notes

7067)
Description:
As a Comply User, the VAT Group Submission Type for the Annual VAT Returns are seeded
within Comply. This is displayed under the VAT Group Submissions in the VAT Group Details
section on the Jurisdiction page and on the Return Details page.
This ensures that the user is aware how to submit the group’s Annual VAT Group returns.
Navigation: Jurisdiction Details > VAT Group Details > VAT Group > Germany/Ireland
1.5. Submission Type Consolidated – VAT Group (VCCMVP-9466)
Description:
As a Comply user, there is an Audit Log in the Consolidated Return showing transactions
associated from the VAT Calculations. This audit log is updated when there is a consolidated
submission type for the VAT Group after which that data is uploaded to the VAT Calculations.
This makes it easier to understand which transactions were not uploaded by a user and have
been automatically assigned from the system.
