Purpose of this section The purpose of this document is to provide guidance and instruction on how Comply users submit Returns for UK using an API as part of HMRCs MTD. It will cover the steps required for Configuring Comply and for both Successful and Failed Submission flows. 1.2. Overview To ensure clients are in Compliance with the Making Tax Digital (MTD) integration, Comply provides an API process which allows them to Submit returns digitally to HMRC. 1.2.1. Return Types All Return Types can be submitted via API. • VAT Returns • Annual Returns VAT – Amendments are not included in this process as a Manual Form is required by HMRC. Please Note: 2. External Configuration (HMRC Authorisation) Comply provides the user with the ability to file Submissions via an API (Digital Filing). The essentially allows the agent (TBI) to represent the client and submit returns on their behalf to HMRC. In order for this to be used, authorisation is required to allow digital communication between TBI and HMRC, which allows returns to be submitted digitally by TBI on behalf of the client. The following actions are required and are external steps which are completed outside of Comply, by TBI users acting as agents on behalf of the client. To set this up, the user (TBI) must complete the following steps: 2.1. The agent (TBI) can read the guidance materials provided on GOV.UK. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/making-tax-digital-how-vat-businesses-and- other-vat-entities-can-get-ready https://www.gov.uk/guidance/use-software-to-submit-your-vat-returns https://www.gov.uk/guidance/agents-use-software-to-submit-vat-returns 2.2. The Agent creates an Agent Services Account. To create this, visit: https://www.access.service.gov.uk/login/signin/creds The agent will need: • A Government Gateway user ID and password. • The Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) for your tax agent firm. • The postcode associated with your UTR. 2.3. The Agent links VAT Clients. The agent must complete the following: • The agent signs into their Agent Services Account. • Agent requests to ask a client to authorise them. • Agent gives client’s details including their VAT registration number (VRN) and VAT registration date. • Agent gets a unique link and sends it to their client in email. • Client receives email from agent and clicks on the link to begin the process. • Client logs in with Government Gateway account and completes identity checks. • Client confirms authorisation for agent to represent them. 2.4. The Agent signs the client up for MTD. To do this, complete the following: • Sign into HMRC online services using agent services account. • Provide client details including VAT registration and client’s business type. • Give and verify agent’s own email address. This is only required once. • Choose whether client prefers to get emails or letters. • Enter client’s business email address. • Tell clients they’ll get a verification email with a link to click on. This will verify their business email address.

This is only required once. • Choose whether client prefers to get emails or letters. • Enter client’s business email address. • Tell clients they’ll get a verification email with a link to click on. This will verify their business email address. The link will expire after 3 days. • Confirm all information is correct before submitting it to HMRC. • Wait to hear if the client is approved. This can take up to 3 days. The agent can now file VAT Returns for their client. 2.5. The Agent Links the Software to HMRC. Businesses and agents using your software to connect to the VAT (MTD) API must grant authority to your software to interact with HMRC on their behalf. We use the open standard OAuth 2.0 (opens in a new tab), which involves the business or agent signing in via their Government Gateway account and following the grant authority user journey. • Business or agent requests to link your software to HMRC • Your software launches the grant authority user journey • Business or agent views the HMRC start page for an overview of the process and chooses to continue • Business or agent signs in with their Government Gateway user ID and password (agents must use their new agent services user ID) • Business or agent registers for or completes 2-step verification as applicable • Business or agent completes identity checks if applicable • Business or agent grants authority for the software to interact with HMRC on their • HMRC generates an OAuth token for the business or agent • Your software stores the business or agent’s OAuth token for later use in API calls on behalf their behalf The first part of this process in Comply is introduced on the Return Review screen where the 3. Filing Obligation After clicking Submit, an Obligation validation is triggered. This checks if the data being submitted is for a required return for that period. An error message is displayed if: • The return for that period has already been submitted. • There is no obligation required for the period details in the submitted file. The following actions are triggered in Comply. • The Status is changed to Submission Failed. • A log in added to the Audit History. 4.3.2. Data Validation may be issues with the data. (This allows the user to make the necessary changes and resubmit the return).
